# Lumen

> Lumen is a TypeScript 7-first web framework: `.stsx` components (TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks), setup-once components with signals, and server-first rendering with islands.

These docs match lumen 0.0.0. Installed projects have them in `node_modules/lumen/docs`;
`lumen docs <topic>` prints one and `lumen explain <code>` explains a diagnostic.

<!-- source: README.md -->

# Lumen docs

> Lumen is a TypeScript 7-first web framework: `.stsx` components (TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks), setup-once components with signals, and server-first rendering with islands.

These docs ship inside the package, so they always match the installed version. Read them from
`node_modules/lumen/docs`, or from the terminal:

```sh
lumen docs                    # this index
lumen docs signals            # a topic, by name or path (concepts/signals)
lumen docs "bind:value"       # search, when no topic matches
lumen explain LUM2001         # the long-form explanation of a diagnostic
lumen docs signals --format json
```

Every concept page has the same sections, in order: **Concept**, **API**, **Example**, **Common
mistakes** and **Related diagnostics**. Reference pages list every export with its signature.

## Start here

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): Create a project, configure TypeScript and Vite, and render a first component.

## Concepts

- [Components](concepts/components.md): Setup-once function components, props, children, refs and the `.stsx`/`.tsx`/`.ts` file types.
- [Signals and reactivity](concepts/signals.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `store`, owners, context and scheduling.
- [JSX](concepts/jsx.md): Bindings, compiled idioms (`.map`, ternaries), `class`, `style`, events, `bind:`, `attach` and `ref`.
- [Styles](concepts/styles.md): Raw-CSS `<style>` blocks scoped by placement, `<style global>`, JS values in styles (`$name`), build-time math and runtime values.
- [Async components](concepts/async.md): `async` components on server and client, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`, re-runs and in-flight state.
- [Islands](concepts/islands.md): `client:*` directives, serializable props, slots and server-only boundaries.
- [Routing](concepts/routing.md): File routes, layouts, params, typed `href()`, error pages and the SPA router.
- [Data and actions](concepts/data-and-actions.md): Read data with async components, serve endpoints, mutate with form actions and `submit()`.
- [Server](concepts/server.md): Request context, middleware, cookies, env, redirects and error helpers.
- [Rendering modes](concepts/rendering-modes.md): `static`, `server` and `spa` routes, shell-first streaming, hydration and the build.
- [SVG imports](concepts/svg.md): `import Icon from "./icon.svg"` as an inline, optimised component; `title`, `currentColor`, `?url` and `?raw`.
- [Markdown and HTML imports](concepts/content.md): `.md` and `.html` files as static components; GFM, heading ids, frontmatter and its hook, scoped `<style>`, client `<script>`.
- [Head and document](concepts/head.md): `<Title>`, `<Meta>`, `<Head>` and a custom `document.stsx`.
- [Compiler and diagnostics](concepts/compiler.md): What the compiler does with `.stsx`/`.tsx`, and how `LUMxxxx` diagnostics work.
- [Testing](concepts/testing.md): Test components with Vitest and the Lumen Vite plugin.
- [Security](concepts/security.md): A strict Content Security Policy with nonces and hashes (`lumen({ csp: "strict" })`, `cspNonce()`), and the cross-site form check.

## Reference

- [`lumen`: reactivity](reference/reactivity.md): `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `batch`, `flushSync`, `untrack`, `store`, owners, context, `pending`, `busy`, `resource`.
- [`lumen`: components](reference/components.md): `Suspense`, `ErrorBoundary`, `Portal`, `Dynamic`, `ref`, `Head`, `Title`, `Meta`.
- [`lumen`: app layer](reference/app.md): `fetchJSON`, `submit`, `submitting`, `actionData`, `invalidate`, `fail`, `redirect`, `notFound`, `error`, `href`, request APIs and types.
- [`lumen`: server rendering](reference/server.md): `renderToStream`, `renderToString` and the `lumen/server` subpath.
- [`lumen/dom`](reference/dom.md): `mount`, the compiler-runtime contract, `hydrate` (`lumen/dom/hydrate`) and the island loader (`lumen/dom/loader`).
- [`lumen/router`](reference/router.md): The SPA router: `Link`, `navigate`, `navigating` and reactive route state.
- [`lumen/vite`](reference/vite.md): The Vite plugin and its options.
- [JSX types and tsconfig](reference/jsx.md): `lumen/jsx-runtime`, `lumen/env` and the required `tsconfig.json`.
- [CLI](reference/cli.md): `lumen dev`, `build`, `preview`, `check`, `typegen`, `routes`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`, `explain`, `agents init` and `mcp`; `--format json` and exit codes.
- [MCP server](reference/mcp.md): `lumen mcp` for coding agents: docs, `check` with fixes, routes, components, compiler output, rendered HTML and dev logs.
- [`@lumen/adapter-node`](reference/adapter-node.md): `createServer`, `createHandler` and `createStaticHandler`: serve a build with Node.

## Diagnostics

- [All diagnostics](errors/README.md): Every `LUMxxxx` code with its explanation and fix.

## Status of this version

Lumen is pre-release (`0.0.0`). The docs describe the designed API; where this version does not
implement something yet, the page says so in a **Status** note. In short:

| Area                                                                                | Status                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Signals, components, JSX compilation, client rendering (`lumen/dom`)                | Available                                                            |
| Async components, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`                                   | Available                                                            |
| Server rendering (`renderToStream`), shell-first streaming, head                    | Available                                                            |
| File routes, typegen, request handler, middleware, actions, `fetchJSON`             | Available, with `lumen dev`, `lumen build` and `@lumen/adapter-node` |
| `<style>` blocks                                                                    | Available                                                            |
| Islands hydration and the island loader                                             | Available                                                            |
| SPA mode and the SPA router (`lumen/router`)                                        | Available, with `lumen dev` and `lumen build`                        |
| `lumen check`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`, `explain`, language server, VS Code extension | Available                                                            |
| `lumen mcp`                                                                         | Available                                                            |
| `create-lumen` (templates `minimal`, `static`, `ssr`, `spa`), `lumen agents init`   | Available                                                            |
| `@lumen/testing`                                                                    | Planned                                                              |

<!-- source: getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

> Set up a Lumen project with TypeScript 7 and Vite 8, write a first `.stsx` component and check it with `lumen check`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 or later.
- TypeScript 7 (`typescript@^7`). Lumen uses stock `tsc`, with no TypeScript plugins.
- Vite 8.

## Create a project

```sh
pnpm create lumen my-app --template ssr   # or: minimal, static, spa
cd my-app && pnpm install && pnpm dev
```

| Template  | `lumen({ mode })` | What you get                                                 |
| --------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `minimal` | `static`          | One page.                                                    |
| `static`  | `static`          | A layout, pages, a blog with `staticPaths()` and a 404 page. |
| `ssr`     | `server`          | Streaming, a form action, a JSON endpoint and a Node server. |
| `spa`     | `spa`             | Pages and a persistent layout rendered in the browser.       |

Every project starts agent-ready: `AGENTS.md` (with a Lumen section pointing at these docs),
`CLAUDE.md` referencing it, the `lumen` skill in `.claude/skills/lumen`, and `.gitattributes`
highlighting `.stsx` as TSX. In an existing project, `lumen agents init` writes the same files
(re-run it after upgrading Lumen; it only touches its own parts). With `--mcp`, both also register
the [Lumen MCP server](reference/mcp.md) for Claude Code (`.mcp.json`) and Codex
(`.codex/config.toml`). Run `create-lumen --help` for the options (`--yes`, `--force`, `--mcp`,
`--format json`).

The rest of this page sets a project up by hand, step by step.

## 1. Install

```sh
pnpm add lumen
pnpm add -D vite typescript
```

## 2. Configure TypeScript

`tsconfig.json` extends the tsconfig that Lumen generates (`lumen check` prints this file when it
is missing, and `lumen agents init` writes it):

```jsonc
{
  // Lumen's compiler options, shadow TSX and route types. lumen dev, build, check and typegen
  // write the generated file; add your own options below.
  "extends": "./.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json",
}
```

- `.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json` sets `jsx: "preserve"` (the Lumen compiler transforms JSX, not
  TypeScript), `jsxImportSource: "lumen"`, bundler module resolution, `strict`, `types:
  ["lumen/env"]`, and the `rootDirs` and `include` entries below. Lumen keeps it current.
- `.lumen/shadow`: TypeScript cannot read `.stsx`, so Lumen writes a masked copy of each one (a
  _shadow file_, same line and column offsets) and `import "./X.stsx"` resolves to it.
- `.lumen/types`: generated route types (`lumen typegen`, run by `lumen check`).
- `lumen dev`, `build`, `check` and `typegen` write `.lumen/`. Before a bare `tsc` in a fresh
  clone, run `lumen typegen`. See [tsconfig](./reference/jsx.md#tsconfigjson).

Add `.lumen/` to `.gitignore`, and `*.stsx linguist-language=TSX` to `.gitattributes` so GitHub
highlights `.stsx` files.

## 3. Configure Vite

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumen from "lumen/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumen()],
});
```

## 4. Write a component

```stsx check file=Counter.stsx
// src/Counter.stsx
import { signal } from "lumen";

export function Counter({ start = 0 }: { start?: number }) {
  const count = signal(start);

  return (
    <button class={{ hot: count() > 5 }} onClick={() => count.update((n) => n + 1)}>
      Clicked {count()} times

      <style>
        button { font: inherit; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; }
        .hot { color: crimson; }
      </style>
    </button>
  );
}
```

- The function body runs **once**. `count()` reads the signal; JSX that reads it updates on its own.
- `<style>` inside the component's JSX is scoped to that component's elements.

## 5. Mount it

```html
<!-- index.html -->
<div id="app"></div>
<script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script>
```

```tsx check file=main.tsx
// src/main.tsx
import { mount } from "lumen/dom";
import { Counter } from "./Counter.stsx";

mount(() => <Counter start={1} />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

Run `pnpm vite` and open the printed URL.

## 6. Check the project

```sh
pnpm lumen check        # typegen + shadow files + tsc + Lumen diagnostics
pnpm lumen lint         # oxlint, .stsx included
pnpm lumen fmt          # oxfmt for the TSX, plus each <style> block
```

`lumen check` maps every TypeScript error in a shadow file back to the `.stsx` line and column.
`--format json` prints machine-readable diagnostics; every Lumen diagnostic has a stable code that
`lumen explain <code>` explains.

## Editor

Install the Lumen VS Code extension (`lumen-vscode`). It adds the `stsx` language and runs the
Lumen language server, which proxies TypeScript 7 for `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.stsx` files and adds:

- CSS features inside `<style>` blocks;
- class completion, definitions and rename that follow placement: the blocks enclosing the
  cursor (never a sibling subtree's), the file's, and the project's global classes (`<style global>`
  blocks and imported global `.css` files);
- `var(--…)` completion of every custom property declared in the project, with its value;
- descriptions of `<style global>` and of Lumen attributes (`client:*`, `bind:*`, `on:*`, `attach`,
  `ref`, `key`), and the snippets `comp`, `acomp`, `route` and `island`;
- the compiler's diagnostics, with the project-wide ones (`LUM4003` server-only imports in the
  client graph, `LUM3012` unread custom properties) that follow the other files' edits;
- hovers on JSX expressions with their execution contract: tracked (re-runs when the signals it
  reads change, which it lists), once, untracked or deferred, and the runtime helper that runs it.

The extension bundles the server (it runs on VS Code's own Node.js) and uses the project's
`typescript`; install `@lumen/language-server` as a dev dependency only to pin the server to your
`lumen` version. See [Compiler and diagnostics](concepts/compiler.md).

## Next

- [Components](concepts/components.md) and [Signals](concepts/signals.md): the component model.
- [Styles](concepts/styles.md): scoping by placement, JS values in styles and build-time math.
- [Rendering modes](concepts/rendering-modes.md): server-first pages with islands.

<!-- source: concepts/components.md -->

# Components

> A component is a PascalCase function that returns JSX. Its body runs once, as setup; signals make the JSX update in place.

## Concept

**Files.** Components live in `.stsx` files (TSX plus raw-CSS `<style>` blocks) or plain `.tsx`
files. A file may export many components. Logic, tokens, endpoints and server code live in `.ts`.

| Extension | Contents                                                              |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.stsx`   | TSX plus `<style>` blocks. Use it for components with styles.         |
| `.tsx`    | Plain TSX. A `<style>` block here is `LUM1006` ("rename to `.stsx`"). |
| `.ts`     | Everything else.                                                      |

**Setup once.** The body of a component runs once per instance. There is no re-render: JSX
expressions that read signals become fine-grained bindings, and only those update. Local variables
are ordinary variables; state that changes lives in [signals](signals.md).

**Props.** Props are the single parameter. The compiler keeps them reactive, even when you
destructure them: `({ title, count = 0 })` is rewritten to reads of `props.title` and
`props.count`, so a parent passing a signal value keeps the child up to date. `...rest` stays
reactive too.

On the server, where nothing is reactive, a prop expression is evaluated **lazily and at most once
per component instance** (decision-28): the first read runs it, later reads reuse the value, and a
prop the component never reads never runs. `<Filters labels={listLabels()} />` queries the labels
once per render however often `Filters` reads `props.labels`. In the browser props stay live: each
read re-evaluates the expression, so keep prop expressions free of side effects.

**Children** are lazy: `children` is evaluated where you insert it. Insert it once; to render
something several times, take a render function as a prop. Named slots are ordinary props that hold
JSX.

**Refs.** `ref` takes a callback `(el) => void`. `ref<T>()` returns such a callback that can also be
read like a signal.

**Async.** Any component may be `async` and `await` data in its body; see
[Async components](async.md).

## API

| API                                     | Use                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `function Name(props) { return <… /> }` | A component. PascalCase, returns JSX.                                           |
| `children` prop                         | Lazy content passed between the tags. Insert once.                              |
| `ref<T>()`                              | A ref callback that reads like a signal (`input()`), `undefined` until mounted. |
| `onMount(fn)`, `onCleanup(fn)`          | Run after mount; run when the component is disposed.                            |
| `<Dynamic component={X} … />`           | Render a component (or tag name) chosen at runtime.                             |
| `<Portal mount={node}>`                 | Render children elsewhere in the document.                                      |

Types: a component's return type is `JSX.Element`. Props are a plain interface; `children?:
JSX.Element` for content.

## Example

```stsx check
import { onMount, ref, signal } from "lumen";

interface Props {
  label: string;
  initial?: string;
  children?: JSX.Element;
}

export function SearchBox({ label, initial = "", children }: Props) {
  const query = signal(initial);
  const input = ref<HTMLInputElement>();

  onMount(() => input()?.focus());

  return (
    <form class="search" onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
      <label>
        {label}
        <input ref={input} bind:value={query} />
      </label>
      <p>Searching for “{query()}”</p>
      {children}

      <style>
        .search { display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; }
      </style>
    </form>
  );
}

export function Page() {
  return (
    <SearchBox label="Books">
      <small>Try “Dune”.</small>
    </SearchBox>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading a signal once in setup and expecting it to update.** `const doubled = count() * 2`
  is computed once. Use a function or `computed`: `const doubled = () => count() * 2`. The compiler
  warns with `LUM2001`.
- **Returning early on reactive state.** `if (!user()) return <Login />` runs once. Put the
  condition in the JSX: `{user() ? <Profile /> : <Login />}` (`LUM2003`).
- **Calling a component as a function.** `{Card({ title })}` skips the component's owner and
  props handling. Write `<Card title={title} />` (`LUM2004`).
- **Inserting `children` twice.** The second insert moves or re-creates the nodes. Take a render
  prop such as `renderItem: () => JSX.Element` instead (`LUM2005`).
- **Writing a signal in the component body.** Setup runs during render; a write there
  (`count.set(…)`) re-triggers bindings mid-render. Write in handlers or effects (`LUM2002`).
- **Expecting React re-renders.** There are no hooks rules and no dependency arrays: nothing
  re-runs except bindings and effects that read signals.
- **`className`, `htmlFor`.** Use `class` and `for`; the React names are type errors.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1006](../errors/LUM1006.md): raw CSS in a `.tsx` file.
- [LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md): stale derived value.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.
- [LUM2003](../errors/LUM2003.md): reactive early return.
- [LUM2004](../errors/LUM2004.md): component called as a function.
- [LUM2005](../errors/LUM2005.md): children inserted twice.

See also: [JSX](jsx.md), [Signals](signals.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/signals.md -->

# Signals and reactivity

> State lives in signals: read with `count()`, write with `count.set(v)`. Computeds derive, effects react, and only the code that read a signal re-runs.

## Concept

Lumen's reactive core is a push-pull signal graph (the alien-signals algorithm). Reading a signal
inside a tracked scope (a JSX binding, a `computed`, an `effect`) subscribes that scope; writing
the signal marks it dirty and re-runs only what depends on it.

- **Reads are synchronous.** `count()` always returns the current value, even right after a write.
- **Writes are batched.** Writes inside a delegated event handler are batched for the duration of
  the handler. Any other write schedules a microtask flush. `flushSync()` flushes immediately.
- **Flush order:** computeds are pulled, then DOM bindings run (parents before children), then user
  effects.
- **Owners.** Every component, effect and root is an _owner_. Owners scope cleanups
  (`onCleanup`), context (`provide`/`inject`), error handling and `lifetime()`. Disposing an owner
  disposes everything created under it.
- **Equality.** A write that is `Object.is`-equal to the current value is not a change. Pass
  `{ equals }` to customize, or `{ equals: false }` to treat every write as a change.
- **On the server** signals are plain cells, computeds run once, and effects never run.

## API

| API                                                         | Shape                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal(value, { equals? })`                                | `s()` reads, `s.set(v)` and `s.update(fn)` write, `s.peek()` reads untracked.                                                               |
| `computed(fn, { equals? })`                                 | `c()` reads. Lazy, cached and glitch-free; `fn` receives the previous value.                                                                |
| `effect(fn)`                                                | Runs after the DOM updates and again when what it read changes. `fn` may return a cleanup. Returns a disposer.                              |
| `onMount(fn)`                                               | Runs `fn` once, untracked, after the owner's DOM is mounted. May return a cleanup.                                                          |
| `onCleanup(fn)`                                             | Runs `fn` when the current owner is disposed or re-runs.                                                                                    |
| `store(obj)`                                                | Deep reactive proxy over a plain object or array: mutate it directly.                                                                       |
| `snapshot(value)`                                           | A deep plain copy of a store, for `structuredClone`, `postMessage` and saving.                                                              |
| `untrack(fn)`                                               | Runs `fn` without subscribing to what it reads.                                                                                             |
| `batch(fn)`                                                 | Groups writes; dependents run once at the end.                                                                                              |
| `flushSync()`                                               | Runs pending bindings and effects now.                                                                                                      |
| `lifetime()`                                                | An `AbortSignal` aborted when the owner is disposed, an effect re-runs, or an async run is superseded. On the server, the request's signal. |
| `createContext(default?)`, `provide(ctx, v)`, `inject(ctx)` | Values passed down the owner tree; they survive `await`.                                                                                    |
| `resource(fetcher)`                                         | Low-level on-demand loading with `loading()`, `error()`, `refetch()`. Prefer [async components](async.md).                                  |

In-flight state (`pending()`, `busy()`, `submitting()`, `navigating()`) is covered in
[Async components](async.md) and [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).

## Example

```tsx check
import { computed, createContext, effect, inject, provide, signal, store } from "lumen";

const Theme = createContext<"light" | "dark">("light");

export function Cart() {
  const items = store([{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 1 }]);
  const discount = signal(0);
  const total = computed(
    () => items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.qty, 0) * (1 - discount()),
  );

  effect(() => {
    document.title = `Cart: ${total().toFixed(2)}`;
  });

  provide(Theme, "dark");

  return (
    <section>
      <button onClick={() => items.push({ name: "Ink", price: 5, qty: 1 })}>Add ink</button>
      <button onClick={() => (items[0]!.qty += 1)}>One more pen</button>
      <button onClick={() => discount.set(0.1)}>Apply 10%</button>
      <p>Total: {total().toFixed(2)}</p>
      <ThemeLabel />
    </section>
  );
}

function ThemeLabel() {
  const theme = inject(Theme);
  return <small>Theme: {theme}</small>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Destructuring or copying a signal's value in setup.** `const n = count()` freezes the value.
  Read `count()` where you need it, or derive: `const double = () => count() * 2` (`LUM2001`).
- **Calling `set` with the same object after mutating it.** `list().push(x); list.set(list())` is
  not a change (`Object.is`). Write a new value (`list.update((l) => [...l, x])`), use `store()`,
  or create the signal with `{ equals: false }`.
- **Writing signals in the component body or in a `computed`.** That is a write during render
  (`LUM2002`). Computeds must be pure; write in handlers and effects.
- **Using `effect` to derive state.** `effect(() => b.set(a() * 2))` adds a frame of staleness and
  an extra flush. Use `computed(() => a() * 2)`.
- **Expecting an effect to run synchronously.** Effects run after the DOM updates. In tests, call
  `flushSync()` after a write before asserting.
- **Module-scope signals in server code.** On the server, a signal at module scope is shared by
  every request. Keep request data in components or context (`LUM4008`).
- **Posting a store to a worker.** `postMessage()` and `structuredClone()` throw on proxies: send
  `snapshot(state)`.
- **Expecting `store()` to wrap class instances, `Map`s or `Set`s.** Only plain objects and arrays
  become reactive; other values are returned as is.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM2001](../errors/LUM2001.md): stale derived value.
- [LUM2002](../errors/LUM2002.md): signal write during render.
- [LUM2007](../errors/LUM2007.md): own signal read in an async body.
- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.

See also: [reference: reactivity](../reference/reactivity.md), [JSX bindings](jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/jsx.md -->

# JSX

> JSX reads like React (`.map()`, ternaries, `onClick`) but compiles to cloned templates with fine-grained bindings. Only expressions that read signals update.

## Concept

**Bindings.** The compiler looks at each JSX expression:

- Literals and plain identifiers are **static**: written once.
- Calls and member access (`count()`, `user.name`, `props.title`) become **bindings** that re-run
  when a signal they read changes, and write only the part of the DOM they own.
- `untrack(() => …)` opts an expression out.

**Compiled idioms.** There are no `<For>` or `<Show>` components; ordinary JavaScript compiles to
the efficient form:

| Source                                              | Compiled to                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{items().map((item, i) => <Row key={item.id} />)}` | A keyed list. `key` is optional (items are keyed by reference otherwise). `i` becomes a reactive index only if you use it.                                                                                                            |
| `item.id === selected()` inside `.map`              | An O(1) selector: a selection change touches two rows.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `{c() ? <A /> : <B />}`, `{c() && <A />}`           | A memoised branch: switches only when the condition flips.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `{count() * 2}`, ``{`#${id}`}``, `{String(x)}`      | Provably text: a text node of the template, updated with `setText` (written once when nothing reactive is read). Applies to sole children and to children between elements; a `const` initialised with such an expression counts too. |
| `{row.label()}`, `{id}`, `{props.title}`            | Maybe text, alone between nodes (or the only child): also a text node of the template, written by `insertText`. Text values update the node in place; nodes, arrays and other values render in a region before it.                    |
| `{fn()}` next to text or another `{…}`              | A dynamic insert (a region), since adjacent text nodes would merge when the HTML is parsed.                                                                                                                                           |

**Elements.**

| Prop                         | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `class`                      | A string, an array, or a `{ name: boolean }` record (nested arrays allowed). `className` is a type error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `style`                      | A string, or an object with **kebab-case** keys, including `--custom` properties. Each key updates on its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `aria-*`, `spellcheck`, …    | Booleans are written as `"true"`/`"false"` (`aria-pressed={false}` renders `aria-pressed="false"`): `aria-*`, `contenteditable`, `draggable`, `spellcheck` and the other enumerated attributes, static or not. Other attributes: `true` adds the attribute empty (`hidden`); `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out. |
| `onClick`, `onKeyDown`, …    | camelCase handlers. Bubbling events are delegated (one listener per type at `document`); non-bubbling ones (`onFocus`, `onMouseEnter`, `onScroll`) get a direct listener.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `on:click`, `on:my-event`    | A native `addEventListener` listener with the exact event name. Use it for custom and web-component events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `bind:value`, `bind:checked` | Two-way binding to a writable signal, on `input`, `select` and `textarea`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `attach={[fn]}`              | Runs `fn(el)` with the element in a tracked scope; it may return a cleanup.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ref={fn}`                   | Called with the element. `ref<T>()` makes a callback you can read like a signal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `innerHTML`                  | Sets unescaped HTML. The lint rule `no-unsafe-html` warns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `key`                        | Allowed on intrinsic elements and components (list identity).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `client:*`                   | Island directives, on components only. See [Islands](islands.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Handlers receive the **native** event, with `currentTarget` typed as the element. There are no
synthetic events.

## API

JSX types come from `lumen/jsx-runtime` (via `jsxImportSource: "lumen"`) and the global `JSX`
namespace from `lumen/env`:

| Type                     | Meaning                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `JSX.Element`            | Anything JSX can render: nodes, strings, numbers, arrays, functions, `null`. |
| `JSX.ClassValue`         | The `class` prop value.                                                      |
| `JSX.CSSProperties`      | The `style` object (kebab-case keys and `--custom` properties).              |
| `JSX.EventHandler<E, T>` | A handler: the native event `E` with `currentTarget: T`.                     |
| `JSX.Ref<T>`             | The value of `ref<T>()`.                                                     |
| `JSX.HTMLProps<T>`       | Props of an HTML element, for wrappers and custom elements.                  |

See [JSX types and tsconfig](../reference/jsx.md) for custom elements and the full rules.

## Example

```tsx check
import { signal } from "lumen";

interface Todo {
  id: number;
  title: string;
}

export function TodoList() {
  const todos = signal<Todo[]>([
    { id: 1, title: "Write docs" },
    { id: 2, title: "Ship" },
  ]);
  const selected = signal(1);
  const draft = signal("");
  const progress = signal(40);

  const add = (event: SubmitEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    todos.update((list) => [...list, { id: Date.now(), title: draft() }]);
    draft.set("");
  };

  return (
    <section style={{ "--progress": `${progress()}%`, "max-inline-size": "40rem" }}>
      <form onSubmit={add}>
        <input bind:value={draft} on:focus={(event) => event.currentTarget.select()} />
        <button disabled={draft() === ""}>Add</button>
      </form>
      {todos().length === 0 ? (
        <p>Nothing to do.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul>
          {todos().map((todo) => (
            <li
              key={todo.id}
              class={["todo", { active: todo.id === selected() }]}
              onClick={() => selected.set(todo.id)}
            >
              {todo.title}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **React prop names.** `className` → `class`, `htmlFor` → `for`, `onclick`/`onKeydown` →
  `onClick`/`onKeyDown` (camelCase after `on`). The wrong forms are type errors.
- **camelCase style keys.** `style={{ fontWeight: 600 }}` is a type error; write
  `{ "font-weight": 600 }`, as in CSS. Numbers get no units: write `"12px"`.
- **Passing a value to `bind:value`.** It needs the signal itself: `bind:value={draft}`, not
  `bind:value={draft()}`.
- **Custom events with `onX`.** `onMyEvent` is not an event prop; write `on:my-event`.
- **Using the index outside the row.** The `i` of `.map((item, i) => …)` is a reactive index that
  belongs to its row; storing it in an outer variable or closure that outlives the row is
  `LUM2006`.
- **Wrapping lists in helper components.** `{items().map(…)}` already compiles to a keyed list;
  there is no `<For>`.
- **`innerHTML` with user input.** It is not escaped. Prefer text children.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM2004](../errors/LUM2004.md): component called as a function.
- [LUM2005](../errors/LUM2005.md): children inserted twice.
- [LUM2006](../errors/LUM2006.md): reactive index escapes its callback.
- [LUM1001](../errors/LUM1001.md): syntax error.

See also: [Components](components.md), [Styles](styles.md), [reference: JSX types](../reference/jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/styles.md -->

# Styles

> Write plain CSS in `<style>` blocks in `.stsx` files. Where a block sits decides its scope: the element that encloses it, the file, or the whole app with `<style global>`. CSS reads JS constants as `$name`, inlined at build time, and constant math is precomputed.

## Concept

**Placement decides scope.**

| Placement                                                                            | Scope                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inside a component's JSX, as a child of an intrinsic element or fragment (any depth) | Its **enclosing element and everything written inside it** in that component, including `.map` callbacks and JSX passed as children there. A block directly under the component's root element therefore covers the whole component. Sibling subtrees are not affected, and it never reaches other components' own templates. |
| File top level (conventionally at the end of the file)                               | Every template in the file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `<style global>` (anywhere a block is valid)                                         | The whole app, unscoped. Usually in the root `_layout.stsx`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

```stsx
export function Panel() {
  return (
    <div class="panel">
      <aside class="side">…</aside>                 {/* not styled by the <style> below */}
      <section class="body">
        <p class="note">…</p>
        <style> .note { color: tomato; } </style>  {/* only this <section> subtree */}
      </section>
      <style> .panel { display: grid; } </style>   {/* the whole component */}
    </div>
  );
}
```

**How scoping works.** Each scope with styles gets a token `data-l-<hash>`, a stable hash of the
file path plus the component name, with one token per style-bearing element. Every element in the
scope carries the token: the whole file for top-level blocks, and the enclosing element's lexical
subtree for blocks inside a component. The last compound of each selector gets `[data-l-<hash>]`,
a +0,1,0 specificity bump. Dynamic classes always work, because no element is pruned.

- `:global(.sel)` leaves a selector unscoped; `:deep(.sel)` scopes only the part before it.
- `@keyframes` names are scoped, and `animation` references are rewritten. A block sees its own
  keyframes, then those of the blocks of enclosing elements (innermost first), then the file's, so
  a nested block can animate with keyframes defined under the component's root. Custom properties
  are not scoped.
- **Class passthrough.** When a parent passes `class` to a child component, the parent's scope
  tokens at that call site travel with it: the file token plus every enclosing style subtree. So
  `.cta { … }` in the parent styles `<Button class="cta" />` wherever `Button` applies
  `props.class`. The child applies it on every element whose `class` value may contain it:
  `class={["btn", props.class]}`, a destructured `class` prop or `...rest`, a helper that gets
  `props` (`class={variantClass(props)}`), or a local value or function built from them
  (`const classes = () => ["btn", props.class]`). A class that reaches the element any other way
  (a module-level variable, a context) loses the parent's scope, so read `props.class` in the
  component. Forwarding works through intermediate components: when `Field` passes its own
  `class` prop on (`<Input class={["field", props.class]} />`), `Input`'s element gets `Field`'s
  tokens and those of `Field`'s caller.
- Within a file, file-level CSS comes first, then component blocks in source order.
- **In the editor**, class completion follows the same scopes: in a `class` attribute it offers
  the classes of the blocks that apply there (innermost first), then the project's global classes
  (`<style global>` blocks and imported global `.css` files), never a sibling subtree's.
  `var(--…)` offers every custom property declared in the project, with its value.

**Blocks are plain CSS:** no Sass, no `lang`, `media` or other attributes (only `global`). CSS
imports, CSS Modules, Tailwind v4 and `.scss` imports still work through Vite.

> **Status:** available. `lumen/vite` serves each file's CSS as a CSS module, and style-only or
> constant-only edits hot-update the CSS without remounting. `LUM3012` (a custom property set in a
> `style` prop that no stylesheet reads) is reported by `lumen build` only.

**In builds**, a page needs few render-blocking stylesheets. `lumen build` merges the stylesheets
every page starts with (the document's, the root layouts', shared components') into one file that
all pages link and browsers cache, then puts each page's own stylesheets after it: inline in one
`<style>` when they total 4 kB or less, else merged into one file for that page. The cascade
order is the same as in dev, where each file's CSS stays a separate stylesheet for HMR. In the
sample apps a first view went from 6–8 stylesheet requests to one, with about 30% fewer CSS bytes (brotli).
Each tag lists the stylesheets it holds in `data-l-css`, so an island or an SPA route that imports
one does not load it again.

### JS values in styles

`$name` and `$obj.key` put a JS value into CSS. The compiler evaluates the reference at build time
and inlines the result, so the output is plain CSS: no runtime lookup and no JS inside CSS.
TypeScript checks each reference like any other expression. Imports used only by `$` references
are removed from the JS output, and editing them hot-reloads the CSS only.

**What a reference can name:** a `const` whose value the compiler can work out without running the
app.

| Declared as                                                                                  | Readable from                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A top-level `const` of the file                                                              | Every block of the file. A top-level block must come after it.                                                   |
| A `const` of the enclosing component                                                         | Blocks inside that component, `<style global>` included.                                                         |
| An `export const` (or `export default`) of an imported `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.stsx` or JSON module | Every block of the importing file: named, default or namespace imports (`$theme.space.md`), re-exports included. |

Imports are resolved the way the rest of the toolchain resolves them: by Vite in `lumen dev` and
builds (aliases included), and like TypeScript in `lumen check` and the editor (relative paths,
tsconfig `paths`, package `exports` and `imports`). An import that cannot be resolved, or that has
no such export, is reported as [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) at each reference.

The value may be built from literals, template literals, arithmetic (`+ - * / % **`, unary `-`),
other constants, and object literals with their members at any depth (`$theme.color.brand`),
including spreads, destructuring, `as const` and `satisfies`. Mark token objects `as const`: a plain
object literal folds too, as written, but only `as const` keeps the JS read-only like the CSS.

**How values are written.** Strings are inserted verbatim, without quotes (`"12px"` becomes
`12px`; for a CSS string, put the quotes inside: `'"→"'`). Numbers are inserted as plain numbers
(`const gap = 8` gives `8`), so give them a unit with `calc($gap * 1px)` (which ships as `8px`, see below) or keep the unit in the
constant (`"8px"`, `` `${gap}px` ``). A bare number where a length, angle or time is required
(`gap: $gap`, `rotate: $angle`) is [LUM3018](../errors/LUM3018.md), with `calc($gap * 1px)` as the
fix: Lightning CSS happens to read a bare length as pixels, but angles and times are dropped, and in
custom properties or math functions the number stays unitless. A unit written after the reference
(`$gap px`) does not attach to it ([LUM3019](../errors/LUM3019.md)).

**What cannot be referenced.** The compiler reports it; the CSS keeps the `$` text, which browsers
ignore.

| Reference                                                                                                   | Diagnostic                      | Fix                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `$space(2)`: a function call, or a `const` holding a function or a call's result (`Date.now()`, `signal()`) | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Compute it as a constant: `calc($space * 2px)` with `const space = 4`, or name the steps: `$space.md`. |
| `$count` where `count` is a `let` (or `var`)                                                                | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Make it a `const`, or pass it at runtime (below).                                                      |
| `$open`, `$props.width`: signals, props, parameters                                                         | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Pass it at runtime (below).                                                                            |
| `$sizes.0`: an array item (`sizes.0` is not JS)                                                             | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | An `as const` object with named keys: `$sizes.sm`.                                                     |
| `$brand-primary`: a hyphen, read as `$brand` minus `primary`                                                | [LUM3009](../errors/LUM3009.md) | `$brand.primary`, or a camelCase constant: `$brandPrimary`.                                            |
| A component's `const` in a block outside it (file level, or another component)                              | [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md) | Move the `const` to the top level, or the block into the component.                                    |
| A top-level block above the `const` it reads                                                                | [LUM3013](../errors/LUM3013.md) | Move the block below it; by convention, to the end of the file.                                        |

`LUM3008`'s message says which case it is (a `let` binding, computed by a call at runtime, an array,
not declared in scope, an import that does not export the name, …).

**Where `$` is read:** in property values (`gap: calc($gap * 1px)`) and in `@media`, `@container`
and `@supports` preludes (`@media (width < $narrow)`). Everywhere else `$` is left to CSS:

- In selectors, `$` keeps its CSS meaning: `[href$=".pdf"]` is "ends with". `.size-$md` is not a
  reference but an invalid selector, which Lightning CSS drops (`LUM3015`).
- Property names, strings (`content: "$gap"`), comments and `url($file)` are not substituted. Put
  the whole value in the constant instead: `const hero = 'url("/hero.png")'` and
  `background-image: $hero`.

**Runtime values.** A `$` reference is fixed at build time. For a value that changes (a signal, a
prop, a measurement), set a custom property with the `style` prop and read it with `var()`. Custom
properties are not scoped and inherit, so descendants can read them too.

```stsx
<div class="bar" style={{ "--fill": `${pct()}%` }}>
  <style>
    .bar { inline-size: var(--fill); }
  </style>
</div>
```

Tokens usually live in their own module:

```ts check file=theme.ts
// src/theme.ts
export const space = { sm: 4, md: 8, lg: 16 } as const;
export const radius = "6px";
export const narrow = "40rem";
```

```stsx check file=components/Meter.stsx
// src/components/Meter.stsx
import * as theme from "../theme.ts";

const track = theme.space.sm * 2;
const shadow = `0 1px ${track / 4}px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)`;

export function Meter(props: { label: string; value: number }) {
  const border = 1;

  return (
    <div class="meter" style={{ "--value": `${props.value}%` }}>
      <span>{props.label}</span>
      <div class="track">
        <div class="fill" />
      </div>

      <style>
        .meter {
          --pad: calc($theme.space.md * 2px);
          display: grid;
          gap: calc($theme.space.sm * 1px);
          padding: var(--pad);
          border: calc($border * 1px) solid;
          border-radius: $theme.radius;
        }
        .track { block-size: calc($track * 1px); border-radius: calc($track * 1px / 2); box-shadow: $shadow; }
        .fill { inline-size: var(--value); block-size: 100%; background: currentColor; }
        @media (width < $theme.narrow) {
          .meter { max-inline-size: calc(100% - $theme.space.lg * 2px); }
        }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The compiler's CSS output for that file (`data-l-lw1tegds` is the component's scope token). Every
`$` reference and every constant `calc()` is gone; only the runtime `var(--value)` and the
`%`-relative width are left to the browser:

```css
.meter[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  --pad: 16px;
  padding: var(--pad);
  border: 1px solid;
  border-radius: 6px;
  gap: 4px;
  display: grid;
}

.track[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  border-radius: 4px;
  block-size: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 1px 2px #0003;
}

.fill[data-l-lw1tegds] {
  inline-size: var(--value);
  background: currentColor;
  block-size: 100%;
}

@media (width < 40rem) {
  .meter[data-l-lw1tegds] {
    max-inline-size: calc(100% - 32px);
  }
}
```

Lightning CSS also minifies values (`rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)` becomes `#0003`) and may reorder or merge
declarations, so the output is equivalent to the source, not identical.

#### Build-time math

Constant math never reaches the browser. It is computed in two steps:

1. **JS math, by the Lumen compiler.** Arithmetic in constants and template literals is evaluated
   before the value is inserted: `const track = theme.space.sm * 2` inlines `8`.
2. **CSS math, by Lightning CSS.** After substitution, Lightning CSS reduces `calc()`, `min()`,
   `max()`, `clamp()`, `round()`, `abs()`, the trigonometric functions and the other CSS math
   functions whenever the operands are concrete values in compatible units. `calc($gap * 2px)`
   becomes `calc(8 * 2px)`, which ships as `16px`.

| Source (`$gap` is `8`)                    | Output                                | Why                                            |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `padding: calc($gap * 2px)`               | `padding: 16px`                       | `calc(8 * 2px)` reduces.                       |
| `inline-size: min(10px, 20px)`            | `inline-size: 10px`                   |                                                |
| `block-size: clamp(4px, 8px, 12px)`       | `block-size: 8px`                     |                                                |
| `transform: rotate(calc(45deg * 2))`      | `transform: rotate(90deg)`            | Math inside other functions reduces too.       |
| `inset: calc(2px + 3px) calc(1rem + 4px)` | `inset: 5px calc(1rem + 4px)`         | Each value on its own: `rem` plus `px` stays.  |
| `width: calc(100% - $gap * 2px)`          | `width: calc(100% - 16px)`            | The constant part reduces; `%` stays.          |
| `font-size: calc(2 * 1rem)`               | `font-size: 2rem`                     | One unit: nothing to convert.                  |
| `font-size: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 3rem)`       | unchanged                             | `rem` and `vw` are only known in the browser.  |
| `max-width: calc(var(--w) + $gap * 2px)`  | `max-width: calc(var(--w) + 8 * 2px)` | A declaration with `var()` is kept as written. |
| `--space: calc($gap * 2px)`               | `--space: 16px`                       | A custom property, folded by Lumen (below).    |
| `padding-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)`   | `padding-left: 0`                     | Negative in a non-negative property (below).   |
| `margin-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)`    | `margin-left: -4px`                   | Margins can be negative.                       |

**What cannot fold.** A math function is replaced only by a value that means the same thing
wherever it is used. Absolute units convert into each other (`calc(1in + 4px)` is `100px`) and a
unit combines with itself (`calc(2 * 1rem)` is `2rem`), but context-dependent units mixed with
others need the browser: `%` resolves against the containing block (or the font size, depending on
the property), `vw` and `vh` against the viewport, `em` against the element's font size and `rem`
against the root's. A `var()` is only known when the browser computes styles, so Lightning CSS keeps
any declaration containing one exactly as written, constant parts included. To precompute those,
do the arithmetic in JS: with `` const extra = `${gap * 2}px` ``, `calc(var(--w) + $extra)` ships as
`calc(var(--w) + 16px)`.

**Custom properties.** Lightning CSS keeps custom property values as written, because it cannot
know where they will be used. Lumen folds each math function in them that reduces to a single value
in compatible units: `--space: calc($gap * 2px)` becomes `16px`, `--turn: rotate(calc(45deg * 2))`
becomes `rotate(90deg)`, and `var(--x, calc($gap * 3px))` becomes `var(--x, 24px)`. Anything with
`var()`, `env()` or context-dependent units mixed with other units stays whole, without the partial
reduction regular properties get (`--inset: calc(100% - $gap * 2px)` stays `calc(100% - 8 * 2px)`).
Negative results and fractional numbers stay inside `calc()` (`calc(-3px)`, `calc(.333333)`),
because a bare value can behave differently where the property is read: `calc()` clamps to the
property's range and rounds where an integer is expected.

**Negative results.** Some properties cannot be negative: padding, sizes (`width`, `min-height`,
…), border widths, `gap`, `font-size`, `line-height` and others. In the browser, a `calc()` that
comes out negative there is clamped to 0, while a negative value written out is invalid and the
whole declaration is dropped. So that folding does not change the meaning, a negative result in such
a property ships as `0`: `padding-left: calc($gap * 1px - 12px)` gives `padding-left: 0`, and
`font-size: calc(1rem - 2rem)` gives `font-size: 0`. This mirrors the upstream Lightning CSS fix
([lightningcss#1329](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/lightningcss/pull/1329)), which Lumen
applies until a release includes it. Properties that accept negative values, such as margins and
`inset`, keep them.

Folding regular properties, minification and browser targets come from
[Lightning CSS](https://lightningcss.dev), the CSS parser, transformer and minifier from the Parcel
project, which Lumen's CSS compiler is built on. Lumen adds `$` constants, scoping and the
custom-property folding.

## API

| Syntax                                   | Meaning                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<style>…</style>` in component JSX      | CSS scoped to its enclosing element's subtree (the whole component when placed under the root element).  |
| `<style>…</style>` at module top level   | File-scoped CSS. Must come after the `const`s it references.                                             |
| `<style global>…</style>`                | Unscoped, app-wide CSS.                                                                                  |
| `$name`, `$obj.key`                      | A JS constant, inlined at build time, in property values and `@media`/`@container`/`@supports` preludes. |
| `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()`, … | Folded at build time when every operand is a concrete value in compatible units.                         |
| `:global(sel)`, `:deep(sel)`             | Escape or extend the scope.                                                                              |
| `style={{ "--x": value }}` + `var(--x)`  | Runtime values.                                                                                          |

## Example

```stsx check
// tokens are usually in their own module: `export const radius = { sm: "4px", lg: "12px" } as const;`
const radius = { sm: "4px", lg: "12px" } as const;
const BREAKPOINT = "40rem";

export function Card(props: { title: string; progress: number; class?: string }) {
  const gap = 12;

  return (
    <article class={["card", props.class]} style={{ "--progress": `${props.progress}%` }}>
      <h2>{props.title}</h2>
      <div class="bar" />

      <style>
        .card { display: grid; gap: calc($gap * 1px); border-radius: $radius.lg; }
        .bar { inline-size: var(--progress); block-size: 4px; background: currentColor; }
        @media (width < $BREAKPOINT) { .card { border-radius: $radius.sm; } }
      </style>
    </article>
  );
}

export function Dashboard() {
  return (
    <main>
      <Card class="featured" title="Uploads" progress={40} />

      <style>
        .featured { outline: 2px solid gold; }
      </style>
    </main>
  );
}

<style>
  h2 { margin: 0; }
</style>
```

`.featured` in `Dashboard` reaches the `<article>` inside `Card` through class passthrough; `h2`
in the file-level block styles every template in the file.

## Common mistakes

- **A block inside `{…}`, a conditional, a `.map` callback, or a component element** such as
  `<Suspense>` or `<Card>`. Move it into an intrinsic element of the component (`LUM3010`).
- **Returning a block, or using it as an expression** (`return <style>…`, `=> <style>`). Put it
  inside the returned element (`LUM3011`).
- **Hyphenated references.** `$brand-primary` reads `$brand` minus `primary`. Use an object
  member: `$brand.primary` (`LUM3009`).
- **Non-constant references.** `$count` where `count` is a signal, a prop or a `let`, or a call
  such as `$space(2)`, is `LUM3008`. Pass runtime values with `style={{ "--count": count() }}` and
  `var(--count)`; replace calls with constant math (`calc($space * 2px)`).
- **Array items.** `$sizes.0` is not JS (`LUM3008`). Use an `as const` object: `$sizes.sm`.
- **A unit after a reference.** `margin: $gap px` ships as `8 px`, which browsers ignore
  (`LUM3019`). Write `calc($gap * 1px)` or keep the unit in the constant.
- **A unitless number in a length, angle or time.** `gap: $gap` with `const gap = 8` relies on
  Lightning CSS reading `8` as pixels, and `rotate: $angle` is dropped (`LUM3018`). Multiply by the
  unit (`calc($angle * 1deg)`) or keep the unit in the constant.
- **`$` in selectors, strings or `url()`.** It is not substituted there (`[href$=".pdf"]` is CSS's
  "ends with"). Put the whole value in a constant, `url()` included.
- **A top-level block before the `const`s it reads.** Move the block to the end of the file
  (`LUM3013`).
- **`<style>` in a `.tsx` file.** It is a type error in `.tsx` (and `LUM1006` for raw CSS); rename the file to `.stsx`.
- **Attributes on `<style>`.** Only `global` is allowed (`LUM1005`).
- **Expecting a parent's styles to reach into children.** Scopes stop at component boundaries;
  pass `class` (passthrough) or use `:deep()`.
- **Expecting a nested block to style sibling subtrees.** A `<style>` inside an element only
  styles that element's subtree. Move it up to the common ancestor, or under the component's root
  element, to cover more.
- **Styling JSX returned by a helper function.** In `const field = () => <label class="field">…`
  inside a component, the helper's JSX is not inside the element that holds a nested `<style>`, so
  `.field` matches nothing there (`LUM3005`). Move the block to the top level of the file (it
  styles every element of the file), or render that JSX inside the styled element.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1004](../errors/LUM1004.md), [LUM1005](../errors/LUM1005.md), [LUM1006](../errors/LUM1006.md): unclosed block, unknown attribute, raw CSS in `.tsx`.
- [LUM3005](../errors/LUM3005.md): unused scoped selector.
- [LUM3008](../errors/LUM3008.md), [LUM3009](../errors/LUM3009.md), [LUM3013](../errors/LUM3013.md): `$` reference problems.
- [LUM3010](../errors/LUM3010.md), [LUM3011](../errors/LUM3011.md): misplaced blocks.
- [LUM3012](../errors/LUM3012.md): custom property set but never read.
- [LUM3014](../errors/LUM3014.md), [LUM3015](../errors/LUM3015.md): CSS syntax error, invalid CSS dropped (such as `$` in a selector).
- [LUM3017](../errors/LUM3017.md): a declaration value browsers would ignore, or no value.
- [LUM3020](../errors/LUM3020.md): an unknown property name, with a fix for close typos.
- [LUM3018](../errors/LUM3018.md), [LUM3019](../errors/LUM3019.md): a unitless `$` number, a unit separated from a reference.

See also: [Components](components.md), [JSX `style` and `class`](jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/async.md -->

# Async components

> Any component may be `async` and `await` data in its body, on the server and the client. `<Suspense>` shows a fallback while new content loads; `<ErrorBoundary>` catches failures.

## Concept

Async components are **the** way to read data in Lumen (there are no route loaders). The same
component works in every rendering mode.

**The await rewrite.** The compiler rewrites `await` only where the nearest enclosing function is
the component itself; awaits inside handlers and callbacks are ordinary awaits. Around each
component-level `await`, the runtime restores the owner, context and tracking, so `inject()`,
`lifetime()` and signal reads keep working after it.

**Re-runs.** Props and signals read in the body (before or after an `await`) are tracked. When one
changes, the component **re-runs**:

- the previous run's `lifetime()` signal aborts (cancel your fetches with it);
- the old UI stays on screen until the new run resolves, then swaps atomically;
- signals created in the body start fresh on each run;
- `pending()` is true while the re-run is in flight.

**Boundaries.**

- `<Suspense fallback={…}>` shows its fallback for **new** pending content: the first load, and
  branches mounted later. Re-runs of content already shown keep the stale UI instead (use
  `pending()` to dim it).
- `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, retry) => …}>` catches rejections and render errors below it.
- With no boundary: on the server the component becomes part of the page shell (the response waits
  for it); on the client nothing renders until it resolves; errors go to the `_error` page.

**In-flight state** (all are reactive and safe to read anywhere):

| Helper              | True while                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pending()`         | this async component's own re-run is in flight (inside the component or its UI).                       |
| `submitting(name?)` | a form action submission is in flight. See [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).                    |
| `navigating()`      | an SPA navigation is in flight. See [Routing](routing.md).                                             |
| `busy()`            | anything above is in flight, or any `<Suspense>` shows its fallback. Use it for a global progress bar. |

**Islands.** Inside an [island](islands.md), each awaited value is recorded during SSR and
replayed during hydration, so the client does not fetch it again. Those values must be plain data
(`LUM4007`), and **everything awaited inside an island is sent to the browser**.

> **Status:** async components, the `await` rewrite, re-runs, `<Suspense>`, `<ErrorBoundary>`,
> `pending()`, `busy()` and server streaming are available, and so is replaying awaited values when
> an island hydrates (see [Islands](islands.md)).

## API

| API                                                              | Shape                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `async function Name(props) { const x = await …; return <… /> }` | An async component.                                                                                       |
| `<Suspense fallback={…}>`                                        | Fallback for new pending content below.                                                                   |
| `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, retry) => …}>`                 | Fallback after an error below; `retry()` mounts the children again. `fallback` may also be plain content. |
| `pending()`                                                      | Whether this component's re-run is in flight.                                                             |
| `busy()`                                                         | Whether anything in the app is in flight.                                                                 |
| `lifetime()`                                                     | `AbortSignal` of the current run; aborted when superseded or disposed.                                    |
| `fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`                                       | Isomorphic JSON fetch that returns plain data. See [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).               |

## Example

```tsx check
import { ErrorBoundary, Suspense, fetchJSON, lifetime, pending, signal } from "lumen";

interface Book {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  summary: string;
}

export async function BookDetails({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const book = await fetchJSON<Book>(`/api/books/${id}`, { signal: lifetime() });
  const expanded = signal(false);

  return (
    <article class={{ stale: pending() }}>
      <h2>{book.title}</h2>
      <button onClick={() => expanded.update((open) => !open)}>Details</button>
      {expanded() && <p>{book.summary}</p>}
    </article>
  );
}

export function BookPage({ ids }: { ids: string[] }) {
  const current = signal(ids[0] ?? "");

  return (
    <main>
      <nav>
        {ids.map((id) => (
          <button onClick={() => current.set(id)}>{id}</button>
        ))}
      </nav>
      <ErrorBoundary
        fallback={(error, retry) => (
          <p>
            Could not load the book ({String(error)}). <button onClick={retry}>Retry</button>
          </p>
        )}
      >
        <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
          <BookDetails id={current()} />
        </Suspense>
      </ErrorBoundary>
    </main>
  );
}
```

Clicking another id re-runs `BookDetails`: the old book stays (dimmed through `pending()`) until
the new one arrives; `<Suspense>` only showed its fallback for the first load.

## Common mistakes

- **Reading the component's own signals in its body.** A signal created in the body and read in
  the body re-runs the component, which re-creates the signal. Read it in JSX or handlers instead
  (`LUM2007`).
- **Not passing `lifetime()` to fetches.** Without it, a superseded run's request keeps going. Pass
  `{ signal: lifetime() }`.
- **Awaiting a `Response` inside an island.** `await fetch(url)` gives a non-serializable value.
  Use `await fetchJSON(url)` (`LUM4007`).
- **Putting secrets in awaited values inside islands.** They are serialized into the HTML. Fetch
  only what the browser may see.
- **Wrapping a re-run in `<Suspense>` and expecting the fallback again.** Revealed content keeps
  its stale UI; show progress with `pending()` or `busy()`.
- **`await using` in a component body.** Not supported in v1 (`LUM1007`).
- **Expecting `resource()` on the server.** It never runs there; use an async component.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1007](../errors/LUM1007.md): `await using` in a component.
- [LUM2007](../errors/LUM2007.md): own signal read in an async body.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch (including replay key mismatches).
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.

See also: [Islands](islands.md), [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/islands.md -->

# Islands

> Pages render on the server and ship no JS by default. Add a `client:*` directive where a component is used, and only that component (an island) hydrates in the browser.

## Concept

An **island** is a component instance that runs in the browser. You declare it at the **usage
site**, so the same component can be static on one page and interactive on another:

```tsx
<TeamPanel client:visible ids={ids} />
```

On the server, the call compiles to an island record: the component's module and export name, its
props, its slots and the hydration strategy. The page HTML contains the server-rendered island
between comment markers (`<!--l:ID-->…<!--/l:ID-->`) plus a JSON record; a small loader (about 1
kB) reads the records, arms the triggers and imports the island's module when one fires. Clicks,
input, submits and key presses that happen before hydration are replayed.

**Directives** (components only):

| Directive                                   | Hydrates                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `client:load`                               | Immediately.                                        |
| `client:idle`                               | When the browser is idle.                           |
| `client:visible` / `client:visible="200px"` | When it enters the viewport (optional root margin). |
| `client:media="(max-width: 600px)"`         | When the media query matches.                       |
| `client:only`                               | Client-rendered only: no server HTML.               |

**Props must be serializable**: JSON values plus `undefined`, `NaN`/`Infinity`, `BigInt`, `Date`,
`URL`, `Map` and `Set`. Functions, symbols, class instances (a `Response` too), promises and cycles
are `LUM4002`.

**Children and JSX props are slots.** They are rendered on the server and stay server components:
they never ship their own JS. A slot the island rendered on the server is adopted in place when it
hydrates; one it did not render yet (behind a condition) is sent as `<template data-l-slot="name">`
and inserted when the island renders it.

**What hydration does.** The island's component runs again in the browser, with the props the
server serialized, and its compiled code claims the server's nodes instead of creating new ones:
the DOM, focus and text selections stay. Awaits replay the values recorded during SSR instead of
fetching again, while still tracking what they read, so a later change re-runs the component and
fetches. Everything outside islands stays server HTML that never hydrates. `client:only` renders on
the client without server HTML. An island inside a streamed `<Suspense>` waits for its content
before hydrating.

**Nested directives.** A `client:*` inside an island's own render is just a component: it is
already client-side.

**Server-only boundaries.** `*.server.ts` files and everything under `src/server/` may not be
imported from code that reaches the browser (`LUM4003`): keep database access, secrets and
`env()` there. `lumen dev` and `lumen build` fail with the chain of importers when the client graph
reaches one, and `lumen check` reports the import. Server-only APIs (`request()`, `cookies()`,
`env()`, …) throw `LUM4003` in the browser build.

**Awaited data** inside an island is recorded during SSR and replayed during hydration, so the
browser does not fetch it again; it must be plain data (`LUM4007`), and it is visible in the page
source. The loader and `hydrate()` are described in [`lumen/dom`](../reference/dom.md).

**The loader script.** `lumen dev` and `lumen build` add the loader to every page that renders an
island, once, as `<script type="module" async>`: in the `<head>` when the shell has islands,
otherwise with the first streamed chunk that does. In a build, pages without islands load no
JavaScript; the loader is the client entry, and each island is a chunk it imports when the island's
trigger fires. The loader's chunk also holds the Lumen runtime the islands share (signals, DOM,
hydration), so a page loads one runtime file before its islands: about 9 to 10 kB min+brotli in
the sample apps (`pnpm --filter lumen size:apps` reports them; the runtime's 10 kB cap is checked by
`pnpm --filter lumen size`). With your own server, pass its URL as
`renderToStream(root, { loaderUrl })`.

**Build output.** `lumen build` puts the Lumen runtime in one chunk: the island loader's, the SPA
entry's when the app has no islands, or a shared `lumen-[hash].js` when it has both. The router's
History API fallback is a separate chunk, loaded only by browsers without the Navigation API. Dynamic
imports go through a smaller preload helper than Vite's: it still adds the imported chunk's
stylesheets (and waits for them, skipping those the page already holds in its merged or inline
styles), module preloads and the CSP nonce of `<meta property="csp-nonce">`, but dispatches no `vite:preloadError` event (the router loads the
URL with a document navigation when a page's module does not load).

**Islands from other packages.** Components of a linked workspace package (`"@acme/ui": "workspace:*"`)
can be or render islands too. Island records name modules without build-machine paths:
root-relative inside the project (`/src/components/LikeButton.stsx#LikeButton`), package-relative
outside it (`@acme/ui/src/Nav.stsx#Nav`), or by the import's bare name
(`import { Nav } from "@acme/ui"` gives `@acme/ui#Nav`). Either way, the `modulepreload` hint of a
`client:load` island points at its chunk in a build and at Vite's URL of the module in dev. Builds
also look for island call sites in the linked packages that depend on `lumen`, so each of their
islands gets its chunk even when only server code renders it. Folders inside such a package that
are projects of their own (with a `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or `vite.config.*`, such as a
showcase app) are left out.

> **Status:** available: island calls and records (`LUM4001`, `LUM4002`), the loader with its
> triggers and event replay, and hydration (`LUM4006` on a mismatch), in `lumen dev` and builds.

## API

| API                                                                           | Use                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible`, `client:media`, `client:only` | Make a component instance an island.                                  |
| `export function X`                                                           | Islands must be exported, so the browser can import them (`LUM4001`). |
| `*.server.ts`, `src/server/**`                                                | Server-only modules.                                                  |
| `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*`                                                    | Env values that may reach islands.                                    |

## Example

```stsx check file=components/LikeButton.stsx
// src/components/LikeButton.stsx: an island; exported so the browser can import it
import { signal } from "lumen";

export function LikeButton({ initial, children }: { initial: number; children?: JSX.Element }) {
  const likes = signal(initial);

  return (
    <button class="like" onClick={() => likes.update((n) => n + 1)}>
      {children} {likes()}

      <style>
        .like { border-radius: 999px; }
      </style>
    </button>
  );
}
```

```stsx check file=routes/posts/[id].stsx
// src/routes/posts/[id].stsx: a server component; only LikeButton ships JS
import { params } from "lumen";
import { LikeButton } from "../../components/LikeButton.stsx";

export default function Post() {
  const { id } = params<"/posts/[id]">();

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Post {id}</h1>
      <LikeButton client:visible initial={3}>
        <strong>Like</strong>
      </LikeButton>
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes
