- **A non-exported island.** `function Counter` used with `client:load` cannot be imported by the
  browser. Export it (`LUM4001`).
- **Passing functions or class instances as island props.** `onSave={() => …}` cannot be
  serialized. Pass data, and do the work inside the island, or post a form (`LUM4002`).
- **Importing server code into an island.** `import { db } from "../server/db.server.ts"` in an
  island's graph is `LUM4003`. Call an endpoint with `fetchJSON` instead.
- **Touching `window` or `document` at module scope** in a module that also runs on the server.
  Move it into `onMount` or an effect (`LUM4004`).
- **Different output on server and client**, for example from `Math.random()` or `Date.now()` in
  render. Hydration reports `LUM4006` in dev and client-renders the range in production.
- **Expecting `submit()` to refresh the page.** On MPA pages a successful `submit()` does not
  reload: the island owns its state and updates itself from the result. Call `invalidate()` when
  the page needs fresh server HTML ([Data and actions](data-and-actions.md)).
- **Making a whole page an island to get interactivity.** Mark only the interactive parts, or use
  an `spa` route ([Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md)).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4001](../errors/LUM4001.md): island component is not exported.
- [LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md): non-serializable island prop.
- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4004](../errors/LUM4004.md): browser API at module scope.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch.
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Async components](async.md).

<!-- source: concepts/routing.md -->

# Routing

> Routes are files under `src/routes`: pages (`.stsx`/`.tsx`), endpoints (`.ts`), nested `_layout` files and `_404`/`_error` pages. Route patterns and params are typed by `lumen typegen`.

## Concept

```
src/
  routes/
    _layout.stsx            root layout; nested _layout.stsx per folder
    index.stsx              /
    about.stsx              /about
    blog/index.stsx         /blog
    blog/[slug].stsx        /blog/:slug
    docs/[...path].stsx     /docs/*  (rest param, may be empty)
    (marketing)/pricing.stsx  /pricing  (a group folder adds no URL segment)
    api/posts.ts            endpoint: export GET / POST / … = (ctx) => Response
    sitemap.xml.ts          endpoint at /sitemap.xml
    _404.stsx  _error.stsx  error pages, nearest one wins
  document.stsx             optional: owns <html>, <head> and <body>
  middleware.ts             optional: export default (ctx, next) => Promise<Response>
```

- **Matching priority:** static segments beat `[param]`, which beats `[...rest]`. Two files for
  the same pattern are `LUM5003`.
- Only `_layout`, `_404` and `_error` may start with `_`; keep shared modules out of `src/routes`
  (`LUM5002`).
- **Layouts** wrap every page below their folder and receive `{ params, children }`. `children`
  is the page (the outlet).
- **Pages** export a `default` component (it may be `async`), which receives `{ params }`. Other
  page exports: `mode`, `ssr`, `staticPaths`, `action`/`actions` and `headers` (see
  [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md) and [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md)).
- **Error pages:** `_404` renders unmatched URLs and `notFound()`; `_error` renders thrown errors
  and `error(status)`. Both receive `{ status, error }`. Outside dev, unexpected errors are masked
  as 500. An error page renders inside the layouts of its folder, like a page there: the root
  `_404` gets the root `_layout` (header, navigation), so it only renders its own content. If a
  layout itself fails, the error page renders without layouts. To give errors a different frame,
  move the regular pages into a group with their own layout (`(app)/_layout.stsx`) and keep the
  error page outside it.

**Typed routes.** `lumen typegen` (run by `lumen check` and the dev server) writes
`.lumen/types/routes.d.ts`, which augments `RouteMap` (pages and endpoints) and `LayoutMap`
(layouts). Every route-bound type then takes the route pattern as a string literal, checked
against that table: an unknown or stale pattern is a type error, and editors complete it.

- `href("/blog/[slug]", { slug })` builds a URL and type-checks the pattern and params; the URL
  includes Vite's `base` and follows `trailingSlash` ([reference](../reference/app.md#href));
- `PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">` types a page's props, `LayoutProps<"/blog">` a layout's
  (`{ params, children }`, with the params of the layout's URL scope; route groups such as `(app)`
  add nothing to it), and `params<"/blog/[slug]">()` the params anywhere on the server;
- `RequestContext<P>`, `ActionContext<P>` and `Endpoint<P>` type `ctx.params` of middleware
  helpers, actions and endpoints (see [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md)).

**Navigation.** Routes are MPA by default: links load the next document. Two `lumen()` options in
`vite.config.ts` make these navigations smooth ([reference](../reference/vite.md#lumen)); both are
progressive, so browsers without support navigate normally:

- **Prefetch** (`prefetch`, default `"hover"`). Pages get `<script type="speculationrules">` that
  prefetches same-origin links: when the pointer rests on a link (`"hover"`), early, as the browser
  sees fit (`"viewport"`), or never (`"none"`). Links to endpoints are never prefetched, since a GET
  endpoint may act (`/logout`). `spa` pages get no rules: there `<Link prefetch>` decides per link.
- **Per link**, `<Link prefetch>` from `lumen/router` overrides the default on MPA pages too. There
  it renders a plain `<a>` (no JavaScript, no router) with a `data-l-prefetch` marker, and the
  rules prefetch it at its own level: `"none"` opts the link out, `"viewport"` prefetches it early,
  `"hover"` on hover. `<Link>` without `prefetch`, like a plain `<a>`, follows the default. The
  server `<Link>` tells the page it rendered a marker as it renders; a hand-written
  `data-l-prefetch` attribute on a plain `<a>` does not change the page's rules.
- **View Transitions** (`viewTransitions: true`, off by default). Every page opts into
  cross-document View Transitions (`@view-transition { navigation: auto }`), except for readers who
  prefer reduced motion: the old page cross-fades into the new one. An element morphs into its
  counterpart on the next page when both have the same CSS `view-transition-name`, unique on each
  page: in a style block (`.site-header { view-transition-name: site-header; }`) or per item with
  ``style={{ "view-transition-name": `cover-${post.slug}` }}``. Style the animation with the
  `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements in a global style block.

```ts
// vite.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [lumen({ viewTransitions: true })] });
```

```tsx
import { Link } from "lumen/router";

// In any page or component: the next page prefetches early, the archive never.
<Link href="/page/2" prefetch="viewport">Older →</Link>
<Link href="/archive" prefetch="none">Archive</Link>
```

Routes with `mode = "spa"` use the client router `lumen/router` ([reference](../reference/router.md)):

- The SPA starts at the outermost `spa` layout (or the page itself) and covers every `spa` page
  below it; links between them navigate on the client, other links load the document.
- `<Link href prefetch>` (plain `<a>` links work too), `navigate(href, { replace })`, reactive
  `params()`, `route()` (the matched pattern), `url()`, `search()` (`search.set()` changes the
  query) and `navigating()`.
- Layouts persist: a layout's `children` is the outlet, and layouts shared by the old and the new
  page keep their state. A page with other param values (`songs/[id]`) is a new page.
- A navigation holds the old page until the new page's async content is ready, then swaps.
- Scroll restoration, focus reset, `_404` for unknown URLs and `notFound()`, `_error` for errors.

> **Status:** file routes, the manifest, matching, typegen, `href()`, the request handler, MPA
> prefetch and View Transitions, and the SPA router (`lumen/router`) are available, served by
> `lumen dev`, `lumen build` and `lumen preview`.

## API

| API                                                              | Use                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `export default function Page(props: PageProps<"/x/[id]">)`      | A page component.                                      |
| `export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/x">)`       | A layout: `{ params, children }`.                      |
| `params<"/x/[id]">()`                                            | The matched route's params, typed by pattern (server). |
| `href(pattern, params?)`                                         | Build a URL from a typed route pattern.                |
| `Routes`, `RouteParams<P>`, `RouteMap`, `LayoutMap`              | Route types.                                           |
| `ErrorPageProps`                                                 | Props of `_404` and `_error`.                          |
| `notFound()`, `error(status, message?)`, `redirect(to, status?)` | Stop rendering; see [Server](server.md).               |
| `lumen/router`: `Link`, `navigate`, `navigating`, `search`       | SPA routes ([reference](../reference/router.md)).      |

## Example

```stsx check file=routes/_layout.stsx
// src/routes/_layout.stsx
import { href, type LayoutProps } from "lumen";

export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/">) {
  return (
    <div class="app">
      <nav>
        <a href={href("/")}>Home</a>
        <a href={href("/blog/[slug]", { slug: "hello-world" })}>First post</a>
      </nav>
      {props.children}

      <style global>
        body { margin: 0; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```stsx check file=routes/blog/[slug].stsx
// src/routes/blog/[slug].stsx
import { Title, notFound, type PageProps } from "lumen";

const posts: Record<string, string> = { "hello-world": "Hello, world" };

export const mode = "server";

export default function Post({ params }: PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">) {
  // A function, so the JSX re-reads it when the params change (a plain const would be LUM2001).
  const title = () => posts[params.slug] ?? notFound();

  return (
    <article>
      <Title>{title()}</Title>
      <h1>{title()}</h1>
    </article>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/_404.tsx
// src/routes/_404.tsx: renders inside routes/_layout.stsx above (its nav and styles), so only
// the page content goes here
import type { ErrorPageProps } from "lumen";

export default function NotFound({ status, error }: ErrorPageProps) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{status}</h1>
      <p>{error.message}</p>
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/index.tsx
// src/routes/index.tsx
export default function Home() {
  return <h1>Home</h1>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Helpers inside `src/routes`.** `src/routes/_utils.ts` or `src/routes/(x).stsx` are not routes
  (`LUM5002`). Put shared modules in `src/lib` or `src/components`.
- **Two files for one URL.** `blog.stsx` and `blog/index.stsx` both match `/blog` (`LUM5003`).
- **Hard-coded URLs.** `"/blog/" + slug` breaks silently when a route moves; `href("/blog/[slug]",
  { slug })` fails type-checking instead.
- **Reading params from `window.location` in a server component.** Use `props.params` or
  `params()`.
- **Matching `url().pathname` to know which route is showing.** `route() === "/songs/[id]"`
  compares the matched pattern, type-checked against the app's routes.
- **Route loaders.** There are none: load data in the async page component itself (decision-18).
- **`mode` that is not a string literal.** `export const mode = getMode()` cannot be read at build
  time (`LUM5002`).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md): invalid route file.
- [LUM5003](../errors/LUM5003.md): duplicate route.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [Server](server.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md), [`lumen/router`](../reference/router.md).

<!-- source: concepts/data-and-actions.md -->

# Data and actions

> One way to read data (async components), one way to serve an API (endpoints), one way to mutate (form actions, enhanced with `submit()`). No route loaders, no RPC server functions.

## Concept

**Reading: async components.** Await data in the component that needs it. Server-only data
access (databases, secrets) lives in `*.server.ts` modules or `src/server/`. See
[Async components](async.md).

**HTTP APIs: endpoints.** A `.ts` file under `src/routes` exports handlers named after HTTP
methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` (and `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`), each
`(ctx) => Response`. Islands, SPA code and other clients call them with `fetch` or `fetchJSON`.

**`fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`** fetches JSON and returns plain data, so awaited results stay
serializable inside islands. Non-2xx responses throw a `FetchError` (an `HttpError` with `status`,
`url` and the parsed body as `data`); if a server component lets it escape, the page renders
`_error` (or `_404`) with that status. **During SSR, same-origin URLs are served in-process**, with
the page request's cookies, without a network round-trip.

**Mutations: form actions.** A page exports `action(ctx)` or named `actions = { name(ctx) }`. A
`<form method="post">` posts to the page (or to `?/name` for a named action) and works without
JavaScript. A named action's URL may keep the page's other query parameters: the action is the
parameter that starts with `/`, wherever it is, so `?status=open&/close` runs `close`, and
`ctx.url` still has `status=open` (useful to redirect back to a filtered list). An action receives
`ctx.formData()` and returns:

| Return                         | Result                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `redirect(to)` or a `Response` | Sent as is (303 after a POST).                                                                  |
| plain data                     | The page re-renders (200) and `actionData()` returns the data.                                  |
| `fail(status, data)`           | The page re-renders with `status`; `actionData()` returns `data`. Use it for validation errors. |

An Origin check protects page POSTs and form-encoded endpoint requests by default (403 for
cross-site requests).

**Enhancing forms.** Inside an island, `onSubmit={submit}` posts the form without a page load.
`submit()` resolves to `{ type: "success", status, data }`, `{ type: "failure", status, data }` or
follows a redirect, and sets `actionData()`. It rejects only for unexpected errors, with a
`FetchError`. `submitting(name?)` is true while a submission is in flight.

**Refreshing.** `invalidate()` re-runs the current page's async components (SPA; the stale UI stays
until the new data arrives), or reloads the page (MPA). On client-routed (SPA) pages a successful
`submit()` runs it for you, so the page shows the mutation without extra code; pass
`submit(form, { invalidate: false })` to keep the page as it is. On MPA pages a successful
`submit()` never reloads: an island owns only its own state, so it updates itself from the result
(`result.data`, `actionData()`). Call `invalidate()` yourself when the page needs fresh
server-rendered content; on MPA pages that reloads and resets `actionData()`.

**Typed results.** Type an action's parameter with its page pattern,
`(ctx: ActionContext<"/books/new">)`, and let TypeScript infer what it returns:
`actionData<typeof actions>()` (or `typeof action`) is the union of the data the actions return
and the data they pass to `fail()`, or `undefined` before a submission. `submit<typeof actions.create>(form)`
resolves with `{ type: "success", data }` or `{ type: "failure", data }` typed from that action,
so the two are told apart by `type`; `actionData()` data is told apart by its shape.
`ActionData<typeof actions>` names that type for a child component's props. An island that posts to another page's action imports the
type only: `import type { actions } from "../routes/reading-list.stsx"`.

## API

| API                                                                | Shape                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/x"> = (ctx) => Response`         | An endpoint method; `ctx.params` typed by the pattern.                 |
| `export const action = async (ctx: ActionContext<"/x">) => …`      | The default form action of a page.                                     |
| `export const actions = { name: (ctx: ActionContext<"/x">) => … }` | Named actions, posted to `?/name`.                                     |
| `ctx.formData()`                                                   | The request body as `FormData` (400 if it is not a form).              |
| `fail(status, data?)`                                              | A failed action result.                                                |
| `actionData<typeof actions>()`                                     | The last action's data or `fail` data, typed by the actions. Reactive. |
| `submit(target, { action?, method?, signal?, invalidate? })`       | Post a form, submit event, `FormData`, `URLSearchParams` or a record.  |
| `submit<typeof actions.name>(…)`                                   | The same, resolving with that action's typed success and failure data. |
| `submitting(name?)`                                                | Whether a submission (to `?/name`) is in flight.                       |
| `invalidate()`                                                     | Refresh the current page's server data.                                |
| `fetchJSON<T>(url, init?)`, `isFetchError(e)`                      | JSON fetch with typed errors.                                          |

## Example

```ts check file=routes/api/books.ts
// src/routes/api/books.ts: GET /api/books?q=…
import type { Endpoint } from "lumen";

const books = [{ id: "1", title: "Dune" }];

export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/books"> = ({ url }) => {
  const q = url.searchParams.get("q")?.toLowerCase() ?? "";
  return Response.json(books.filter((book) => book.title.toLowerCase().includes(q)));
};
```

```stsx check file=routes/books/new.stsx
// src/routes/books/new.stsx: a form that works without JS, enhanced when it hydrates
import { actionData, fail, redirect, submit, submitting, type ActionContext } from "lumen";

interface Errors {
  title?: string;
}

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async create(ctx: ActionContext<"/books/new">) {
    const form = await ctx.formData();
    const title = String(form.get("title") ?? "").trim();
    if (title === "") return fail(400, { title: "A title is required." } satisfies Errors);
    // await db.books.insert({ title });
    redirect("/books");
  },
};

export function NewBookForm() {
  return (
    <form method="post" action="?/create" onSubmit={submit}>
      <input name="title" />
      <p class="error">{actionData<typeof actions>()?.title}</p>
      <button disabled={submitting("create")}>Add book</button>
    </form>
  );
}

export default function NewBook() {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>New book</h1>
      <NewBookForm client:load />
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check
import { fetchJSON, isFetchError } from "lumen";

export async function BookSearch({ q }: { q: string }) {
  try {
    const books = await fetchJSON<{ id: string; title: string }[]>(
      `/api/books?q=${encodeURIComponent(q)}`,
    );
    return (
      <ul>
        {books.map((book) => (
          <li key={book.id}>{book.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if (isFetchError(error) && error.status === 404) return <p>No books.</p>;
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Keeping the page's filters through a named action:

```stsx check file=routes/issues.stsx
// src/routes/issues.stsx: the list is filtered by ?status=; "Close" keeps the filter
import { redirect, url, type ActionContext } from "lumen";

export const mode = "server";

export const actions = {
  async close(ctx: ActionContext) {
    // await db.issues.close((await ctx.formData()).getAll("ids"));
    const back = new URL(ctx.url);
    back.searchParams.delete("/close"); // the action key; the filters stay
    redirect(back.pathname + back.search);
  },
};

export default function Issues() {
  const search = url().search; // "?status=open", or ""
  return (
    <form method="post" action={`${search === "" ? "?" : `${search}&`}/close`}>
      {/* rows with <input type="checkbox" name="ids" value={id} /> */}
      <button>Close selected</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Route loaders.** Lumen has none. Await data in the page component; it is the same code on every
  route mode.
- **Calling server code from an island.** Import nothing from `*.server.ts` in island code
  (`LUM4003`); expose an endpoint and call it with `fetchJSON`.
- **`fetch()` instead of `fetchJSON()` inside islands.** A `Response` is not serializable
  (`LUM4007`).
- **Expecting `submit()` to reject on validation errors.** `fail()` resolves with
  `{ type: "failure" }`; only unexpected errors reject.
- **Calling `invalidate()` after a successful `submit()` on an SPA page.** `submit()` already did;
  a second call refreshes twice.
- **Expecting an MPA page to refresh after `submit()`.** On MPA pages `submit()` never reloads.
  Update the island from the result (a toggle sets its own state, a list removes its own row), or
  call `invalidate()` explicitly if the page must show fresh server HTML.
- **Forms without `method="post"`.** Actions only run for POST; `submit()` refuses a form that does
  not say `method="post"`, as the no-JS form would not post either.
- **Throwing for validation errors.** A thrown error renders `_error`. Return `fail(400, data)`.
- **Casting action data.** `actionData<{ errors: … }>()` is a type error: pass `typeof actions`.
  Annotating the export with `Action` (`export const action: Action = …`) hides what it returns,
  so annotate the parameter instead, or check it with `satisfies Action<"/x">`. Add
  `satisfies YourFailure` to `fail()` data whose string literals should stay literal.
- **Disabling the Origin check to make a cross-site form work.** Allow the specific origin instead
  (`csrf.allowedOrigins` in the request handler options).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4007](../errors/LUM4007.md): non-serializable awaited value.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.

See also: [Server](server.md), [Routing](routing.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: concepts/server.md -->

# Server

> Server code gets the request context everywhere: `ctx` in middleware, endpoints and actions, and `request()`, `url()`, `params()`, `route()`, `locals()`, `cookies()` and `response()` anywhere during a server render.

## Concept

**Request context.** Middleware, endpoints and actions receive
`ctx = { request, url, params, locals, cookies, env }`. During a server render, the same values are
available through functions scoped to the current request (they work after `await` too):
`request()`, `url()`, `params()`, `route()` (the matched pattern), `locals()`, `cookies()`,
`response()` and `env(name)`.

**Middleware.** `src/middleware.ts` default-exports `(ctx, next) => Promise<Response>` (or an array,
run in order). Use it for sessions, auth and headers. Put request data on `ctx.locals`, and type it
by augmenting `Locals`:

```ts
declare module "lumen" {
  interface Locals {
    user: { id: string; name: string } | null;
  }
}
```

**Control flow.** `redirect(to, status?)`, `notFound()` and `error(status, message?)` throw; the
framework turns them into a redirect or the nearest `_404`/`_error` page. Without a status,
`redirect()` uses 302 for GET/HEAD and 303 for other methods.

**Cookies.** `cookies.get/getAll/set/delete`. Defaults: `path=/`, `httpOnly`, `sameSite=lax`, and
`secure` on HTTPS and in production. `signedCookie(name)` signs values with HMAC-SHA256 (secret:
`LUMEN_SECRET`, or rotate with an array of secrets); signing protects integrity, not
confidentiality.

**Status and headers.** `response().setStatus()` and `setHeader()` change the page response, and
a page may export `headers(ctx)`. They are writable **until the shell is sent** (see
[Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md)); a change inside a streamed `<Suspense>` boundary is
`LUM5004`.

**Env.** `env("NAME")` reads server env variables (the adapter's env, else `process.env`) in
server-only code. Only `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_*` reaches client code; `publicEnv()` returns that
subset.

**Server-only code** lives in `*.server.ts` modules and under `src/server/`. Importing it from code
that reaches the browser is `LUM4003`.

> **Status:** the request handler, middleware, endpoints, cookies, env and error pages are
> available, served by `lumen dev` and by the build output (`lumen preview`,
> [`@lumen/adapter-node`](../reference/adapter-node.md)).

## API

| API                                                                      | Use                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RequestContext<P>` (`ctx`)                                              | `{ request, url, params, locals, cookies, env }`.                      |
| `Middleware`                                                             | `(ctx, next) => Response \| Promise<Response>`.                        |
| `request()`, `url()`, `params<P>()`, `route()`, `locals()`, `cookies()`  | Request APIs during a server render.                                   |
| `response()`                                                             | `{ status, setStatus, getHeader, setHeader }` until the shell is sent. |
| `redirect(to, status?)`, `notFound(message?)`, `error(status, message?)` | Throw to stop rendering.                                               |
| `isRedirect(e)`, `isHttpError(e)`                                        | Recognize those when you catch errors.                                 |
| `signedCookie(name, options?)`                                           | `{ get(cookies), set(cookies, value), delete(cookies) }`.              |
| `env(name)`, `publicEnv(source?)`                                        | Server env; the `PUBLIC_*` subset.                                     |
| `Locals`                                                                 | Interface to augment with your request data.                           |

## Example

```ts check file=middleware.ts
// src/middleware.ts
import { signedCookie, type Middleware } from "lumen";

const session = signedCookie("session");

declare module "lumen" {
  interface Locals {
    userId: string | null;
  }
}

const middleware: Middleware = async (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.locals.userId = (await session.get(ctx.cookies)) ?? null;
  if (ctx.url.pathname.startsWith("/account") && ctx.locals.userId === null) {
    return Response.redirect(new URL("/login", ctx.url), 303);
  }
  const res = await next();
  res.headers.set("x-frame-options", "DENY");
  return res;
};

export default middleware;
```

```tsx check file=routes/account.tsx
// src/routes/account.tsx
import { locals, redirect, response } from "lumen";

export const mode = "server";

export default function Account() {
  const { userId } = locals();
  if (userId === null) redirect("/login");
  response().setHeader("cache-control", "private, no-store");

  return <h1>Signed in as {userId}</h1>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading request APIs in a `static` route.** `cookies()`, `request()` and friends throw
  `LUM5001` while prerendering. Set `export const mode = "server"`.
- **Setting headers or status after the shell.** Inside a streamed `<Suspense>` boundary it is too
  late (`LUM5004`). Do it before the boundary, in the page body outside `<Suspense>`, in
  `headers(ctx)` or in middleware.
- **Reading secrets with `import.meta.env`.** Only `PUBLIC_*` values exist there. Use `env("NAME")`
  in server-only modules.
- **Catching `redirect()` by accident.** It throws. In a `try`/`catch`, rethrow when
  `isRedirect(error) || isHttpError(error)`.
- **Storing request data in module-scope variables.** Modules are shared by every request. Use
  `locals`, context or component state (`LUM4008`).
- **Expecting signed cookies to hide data.** They are tamper-proof, not encrypted.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph.
- [LUM4008](../errors/LUM4008.md): module-scope signal written during SSR.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.

See also: [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md), [Routing](routing.md), [reference: app layer](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: concepts/rendering-modes.md -->

# Rendering modes

> Each route picks a mode: `static` (built HTML, the default), `server` (rendered per request, shell first, then streamed `<Suspense>` boundaries) or `spa` (a client-routed subtree). All three use the same components.

## Concept

| Mode               | HTML                                                               | JS shipped        | Navigation                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `static` (default) | At build time, for each path from `staticPaths()`                  | Islands only      | MPA (prefetch, opt-in View Transitions) |
| `server`           | Per request: the shell, then streamed boundaries                   | Islands only      | MPA (prefetch, opt-in View Transitions) |
| `spa`              | Server-rendered and hydrated, or a client shell with `ssr = false` | The whole subtree | Client router (`<Link prefetch>`)       |

A route sets `export const mode = "server"` (a string literal); pages inherit the mode of their
nearest layout that sets one, else the project default set in `vite.config.ts` with
`lumen({ mode: "server" })` (`"static"` when unset). `export const ssr = false` applies to `spa`
routes: the build emits a static shell and the page renders in the browser. `lumen({ ssr: false })`
makes that the default for every `spa` route, so `lumen({ mode: "spa", ssr: false })` turns the
whole project into a client-rendered SPA built as static files.

**Shell first, then stream (server mode).**

1. **Shell.** The response starts once everything **outside** `<Suspense>` has resolved, including
   async components without a boundary. Until then you can still set the status, headers and
   cookies, call `redirect()`, `notFound()` or `error()`, and add `<Title>`/`<Meta>`/`<Head>`.
   A failure renders `_error` with the right status.
2. **Stream.** `<Suspense>` boundaries then stream in as they resolve, out of order, and replace
   their fallbacks (with native `<template for>` updates or a ~300 B `$swap` script). An error
   renders the boundary's `<ErrorBoundary>` in place. A head or status change inside a streamed
   boundary is `LUM5004`.
3. **SSG and prerender** resolve everything: no fallbacks and no swap scripts.

So: put slow, optional content inside `<Suspense>` to send the page sooner; leave essential
content (and anything that decides the status) outside.

**Hydration.** Only islands and SPA subtrees hydrate. The compiled code has a single DOM walk;
importing `lumen/dom/hydrate` (done by the island loader and SPA entries) makes it claim existing
server nodes instead of creating them, so bundles without hydration carry no hydration code.
Markers are comments, used only for blocks, branches, text separators and async ranges.

**SPA mode.** An `spa` subtree starts at the outermost `spa` layout of a page (or at the page
itself) and renders as a single root island: layouts above it render on the server only. Its props
come from serializable route data; `request`, `cookies` and `locals` are not passed in. SPA code
calls endpoints instead. Pages with an SPA load the SPA entry (the client route table, a lazy
chunk per SPA layout and page, and the island loader) and navigate with
[`lumen/router`](../reference/router.md). In a build, the page also modulepreloads the chunks of
its SPA layouts and page (and their imports), so a deep link fetches them alongside the entry
instead of after it has run. When nothing in a build hydrates (every SPA page is
`ssr = false` and the app has no islands), the SPA entry starts the router without the island
loader, and the build ships no hydration code.

- **`ssr` (the default):** the server renders the island and the browser hydrates it, replaying
  the server's awaited data.
- **`ssr = false`:** the server sends a shell (the document, the layouts above the SPA and an
  empty island) without loading the SPA's modules, so they may use browser APIs at module scope;
  the browser renders the island. Such pages cannot export `action` or `headers`: use endpoints.
- `_404` and `_error` pages below an `spa` layout render inside the SPA too.

**Build (`lumen build`).** 1. client build (islands, SPA, CSS, assets, `public/`), 2. server
build, 3. prerender of every `static` route (each `staticPaths()` entry for routes with params) and
every static `GET` endpoint, in-process through the built handler and fully resolved (no fallbacks
or swap scripts), 4. precompression: a `.br` and a `.gz` copy next to every text file of
`dist/client` of at least 1 kB, which `@lumen/adapter-node` (and most static hosts and CDNs) serve
to browsers that accept them. Output:

- `dist/client`: assets and prerendered files. Assets include those only server-rendered code
  imports (`import photo from "./photo.png"` in a route, a relative `<img src>` in a `.md`
  import), written once under `assets/` with the fingerprinted URL the HTML uses. Prerendered
  files are `path/index.html` (`path.html` with
  `lumen({ trailingSlash: "never" })`), endpoint files such as `sitemap.xml`, the shell of each
  `ssr = false` page without params, and `404.html` from the root `_404` when the root scope is
  static or `spa`. In an `ssr = false` SPA, `404.html` is the shell: a static host that serves it
  for unknown URLs gets deep links to every route. Vite's `base` applies to URLs, not to file
  paths.
- `dist/server/entry.js`: `export default { fetch }`, plus `createHandler({ env })` and `config`.

A route that reads the request while it prerenders (`cookies()`, `locals()`, `request()`,
`response()`, `url().searchParams`) stops the build with [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md); a static
endpoint can only export `GET` ([LUM5005](../errors/LUM5005.md)). Middleware still runs. A form
post to a prerendered page reaches its `action` on the server. Serve the build with
`@lumen/adapter-node` (`createServer({ port })`: `dist/client` with caching headers, then the
handler) or `lumen preview`. A site whose every route is prerendered (no `server` route, no
server-rendered `spa` route, no form action; `ssr = false` routes with params need a `404.html`
shell) builds no `dist/server`: deploy `dist/client` to any static host, and `lumen preview` serves
it without the adapter. Set response headers once with `lumen({ headers })`
([lumen/vite](../reference/vite.md#lumen)).

> **Status:** `lumen dev`, `lumen build`, prerendering,
> [`@lumen/adapter-node`](../reference/adapter-node.md), CSS links in built pages, the island
> loader (hydration), SPA mode (one root island, `ssr = false` shells) and the SPA router are
> available.

## API

| API                                                 | Use                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `export const mode = "static" \| "server" \| "spa"` | The route's mode (inherited from layouts).                                          |
| `export const ssr = false`                          | `spa` routes: render in the browser only.                                           |
| `lumen({ mode, ssr })` in `vite.config.ts`          | The project defaults for routes and layouts that do not set them.                   |
| `export async function staticPaths()`               | `static` routes with params: `[{ params: { slug: "a" } }, …]`.                      |
| `export function headers(ctx)`                      | Response headers for the page.                                                      |
| `<Suspense fallback>`                               | Marks content that may stream after the shell.                                      |
| `renderToStream(root, options?)`                    | The server renderer behind it all; see [reference: server](../reference/server.md). |

## Example

```stsx check file=routes/stats.stsx
// src/routes/stats.stsx: the shell (title, heading) is sent first; the slow chart streams in
import { Suspense, Title } from "lumen";

export const mode = "server";

async function SlowChart() {
  const points = await new Promise<number[]>((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve([3, 1, 4]), 500));
  return <p>Points: {points.join(", ")}</p>;
}

export default function Stats() {
  return (
    <main>
      <Title>Stats</Title>
      <h1>Stats</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading chart…</p>}>
        <SlowChart />
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/docs/[slug].tsx
// src/routes/docs/[slug].tsx: prerendered for each slug
import type { PageProps } from "lumen";

const pages = { intro: "Introduction", setup: "Setup" } as const;

export async function staticPaths() {
  return Object.keys(pages).map((slug) => ({ params: { slug } }));
}

export default function Doc({ params }: PageProps<"/docs/[slug]">) {
  return <h1>{pages[params.slug as keyof typeof pages]}</h1>;
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Request APIs in a `static` route.** `cookies()`, `request()`, `locals()` and actions need
  `mode = "server"` (`LUM5001`).
- **Setting status or `<Title>` inside `<Suspense>`.** It arrives after the shell was sent
  (`LUM5004`). Decide them outside the boundary.
- **Wrapping the whole page in `<Suspense>`.** The shell is then just the fallback, and the status
  cannot change. Wrap only slow, optional parts.
- **Expecting `spa` routes to receive `cookies` or `locals` as props.** They are not serializable
  into the SPA (`LUM4002`); call an endpoint.
- **Computing `mode` at runtime.** `mode` must be a string literal (`LUM5002`).

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md): non-serializable island prop.
- [LUM5001](../errors/LUM5001.md): request API used during prerender.
- [LUM5002](../errors/LUM5002.md): invalid route file.
- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.
- [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md): hydration mismatch.

See also: [Islands](islands.md), [Async components](async.md), [Head and document](head.md).

<!-- source: concepts/svg.md -->

# SVG imports

> `import Icon from "./icon.svg"` gives an inline SVG component: optimised at build time, styled with `currentColor` and props, labelled with `title`, the same on the server, the client and in islands. `?url` and `?raw` keep Vite's meaning.

## Concept

With the Lumen Vite plugin, an `.svg` file in your project imports as a component. The build
optimises the file with [SVGO](https://svgo.dev) and compiles it into a static template, so
rendering an icon clones markup, on the server and in the browser alike. The icon is
**inline**: its paths are part of the page's HTML, CSS reaches them, and nothing is fetched.

- **Props override the file.** The file's root attributes (`width`, `height`, `viewBox`, `fill`,
  `stroke`, `class`, …) are defaults; any `<svg>` prop you pass replaces the matching one:
  `class`, `style`, `width`, `height`, `fill`, `aria-*`, events and `ref`. The defaults other
  than `class` and `style` stay in the cloned template, so rendering an icon only sets the props
  you pass.
- **Colour.** Icons drawn with `currentColor` follow the text colour (`color` in CSS). For icons
  with a hard-coded colour, set `lumen({ svg: { currentColor: true } })` to replace every colour
  with `currentColor`, or pass `fill`/`stroke` props.
- **Accessibility.** Without `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, an icon is decorative
  and gets `aria-hidden="true"`. `title="Home"` renders `<title>` as the first child, with
  `role="img"` and `aria-labelledby` pointing at it. The id comes from the file and the title
  text, so the server and the client agree without a counter. The file's own `<title>` is
  dropped: the prop is the label.
- **What the build removes.** Scripts, event attributes (`onload`), `javascript:` URLs,
  comments and editor metadata always, whatever the SVGO config; redundant markup when
  optimising. Ids get a per-file prefix, and so do the references to them (`href="#id"`,
  `url(#id)`, `<style>` selectors); class names get it too when the file has a `<style>`. Icons
  never clash with each other or with the page.
- **Optimisation.** By default SVGO runs its `preset-default` plus `convertStyleToAttrs` (fewer
  `style` attributes, for strict CSPs). Pass your own SVGO config as `optimize` to choose the
  plugins (`{ plugins: [...] }`, `multipass`, `floatPrecision`), or `false` to skip SVGO.
- **Query switches.** `./icon.svg` and `./icon.svg?inline` are the component. `?url` is Vite's
  asset URL (or a `data:` URL for small files) and `?raw` the file's text.
- **Dependencies.** `.svg` files under `node_modules` (the plugin's `exclude`) keep Vite's URL
  import, which is what a library importing an `.svg` expects. `lumen({ svg: false })` leaves
  every `.svg` import to Vite.

Inline is a deliberate choice over sprites (`<use href="#id">`): with the compression every
server applies, a page of repeated inline icons transfers about as many bytes as a sprite, and
inline icons render faster and can be styled and animated part by part.

## API

| Import / option                          | Gives                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `import Icon from "./icon.svg"`          | `(props: JSX.SVGProps<SVGSVGElement> & { title?: string })` |
| `import Icon from "./icon.svg?inline"`   | The same component                                          |
| `import url from "./icon.svg?url"`       | The asset URL (`string`, Vite)                              |
| `import text from "./icon.svg?raw"`      | The file's text (`string`, Vite)                            |
| `lumen({ svg: { optimize: config } })`   | Optimise with your SVGO config instead of Lumen's           |
| `lumen({ svg: { optimize: false } })`    | Skip SVGO (sanitising and id prefixes still run)            |
| `lumen({ svg: { currentColor: true } })` | Replace every colour with `currentColor`                    |
| `lumen({ svg: false })`                  | `.svg` imports stay Vite's URLs                             |

The types come with `lumen/env` (`"types": ["lumen/env"]` in `tsconfig.json`).

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts: your own SVGO plugins (optional)
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import lumen from "lumen/vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    lumen({
      svg: { optimize: { multipass: true, plugins: ["preset-default", "removeDimensions"] } },
    }),
  ],
});
```

```tsx
// src/components/Nav.stsx
import Home from "../icons/home.svg";
import Search from "../icons/search.svg";
import logoUrl from "../icons/logo.svg?url";

export function Nav() {
  return (
    <nav>
      <img src={logoUrl} alt="Acme" width={96} height={24} />
      <a href="/" class="link">
        <Home class="icon" /> Home
      </a>
      <button type="button">
        <Search class="icon" title="Search" />
      </button>
      <style>
        .link { color: rebeccapurple; }
        .icon { width: 1.25em; height: 1.25em; vertical-align: -0.2em; }
        .link:hover .icon { color: crimson; }
      </style>
    </nav>
  );
}
```

The `Home` icon is decorative (its link has text); the search button has no text, so its icon
gets a `title`. Both follow the link or button colour through `currentColor`, and `class="icon"`
receives the component's scope, so the scoped `.icon` rule applies.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting a URL.** Before Lumen, `import icon from "./icon.svg"` was a URL string in Vite.
  Use `./icon.svg?url` for `<img src>` and CSS, or `lumen({ svg: false })` for the old behaviour
  everywhere.
- **Loading `vite/client` types first.** `vite/client` also declares `*.svg` (as a string), and
  whichever comes first in `"types"` wins: `Icon` then "cannot be used as a JSX component". List
  `lumen/env` first, or drop `vite/client` (`lumen/env` already types `import.meta.env`).
  Both type `*.svg` with a default export, a duplicate that TypeScript reports in the two `.d.ts`
  files unless `skipLibCheck` is on (the generated tsconfig sets it).
- **Styling inner paths from a scoped block.** The paths belong to the icon component, so only the
  root `<svg>` (through `class`) carries your component's scope. Use inherited properties
  (`color`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`) on the root, or `:deep(path)`.
- **Setting only `width`.** The file's `height` stays, and the drawing is centred in that box.
  Pass both, or size icons with CSS as above.
- **Labelling a decorative icon.** An icon next to visible text needs no `title`; a `title` there
  makes screen readers repeat the text.
- **Hard-coded colours in an icon set.** If icons stay black whatever `color` says, the files
  hard-code a colour: use `lumen({ svg: { currentColor: true } })` for monochrome sets. It runs
  SVGO's `convertColors` before your own plugins, so with a custom config it still applies.
- **Removing `viewBox` in a custom SVGO config.** Without `viewBox` an icon no longer scales with
  `width`/`height`; SVGO's `preset-default` keeps it, `removeViewBox` drops it.

## Related diagnostics

A file that is not well-formed SVG fails the build with its location
(`icon.svg: invalid SVG: … at 3:12`), as does a file whose root element is not `<svg>`.

See also: [Styles](styles.md), [JSX](jsx.md), [reference: `lumen/vite`](../reference/vite.md), [reference: JSX types](../reference/jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/content.md -->

# Markdown and HTML imports

> With `lumen({ md: true, html: true })`, `import Post, { frontmatter, headings } from "./post.md"` and `import Card from "./card.html"` give static components, compiled at build time: CommonMark + GFM with heading ids, a headings list and YAML frontmatter, or HTML whose `<style>` is scoped to the file and whose `<script>` runs in the browser.

## Concept

Both are opt-in options of the Vite plugin. A `.md` or `.html` file in your project then imports
as a component that renders the file's content. The build compiles it into a static template,
like any `.stsx` markup, so it costs a clone in the browser and a string on the server. It works
the same in `static`, `server` and `spa` routes and inside islands.

**Markdown** is plain CommonMark with the GitHub extensions: tables, strikethrough, task lists,
autolinks (`www.example.com`, bare URLs) and footnotes. There is no MDX: Markdown cannot use
components or JS expressions. Raw HTML is allowed, since the file is part of your project, and
follows the HTML rules below, except for `<script>`: Markdown is content only, so a `<script>`
fails the build ([LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md)). Put scripts in an `.html` import or a
component.

- **Heading ids.** Each heading gets a GitHub-style id from its text: `## Hello, World!` becomes
  `id="hello-world"`, and repeats get `-1`, `-2`. A heading written as raw HTML with its own `id`
  keeps it.
- **Frontmatter.** A leading block between `---` lines is YAML (1.2 core schema: dates stay
  strings). The module exports it as `frontmatter`: plain data, `{}` without a block, typed
  `Frontmatter` (any keys, `unknown` values). Lumen has no schema conventions. To validate or transform it at build time, pass a hook:
  `lumen({ md: { frontmatter(data, { file }) { …; return data } } })`. What the hook returns is
  exported (returning `undefined` keeps `data`), and it may be async. A hook that throws fails the
  build with the file's name. Values may be JSON data, `Date`, `URL`, `Map`, `Set`, `BigInt`,
  `undefined` or `RegExp`.
- **Headings list.** The module also exports `headings`: each heading's `depth` (1 to 6), `text`
  and `id`, in document order, raw HTML headings included. The ids are the rendered anchors', so
  a table of contents links with `#${id}`. A heading whose text has no slug (`## !!!`) has no id
  and is not listed.
- **Code blocks** render as `<pre><code class="language-js">`, without highlighting.

**HTML** files are parsed the way a browser parses them.

- **Documents and fragments.** A full document (a doctype, or an `<html>`, `<head>` or `<body>`
  tag) contributes the content of its `<body>`, plus the `<style>` elements and scripts of its
  `<head>`. The rest of the head (`<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`) is dropped. Anything else is a
  fragment and is used as it is. The root `index.html` and other HTML entries of Vite, and files in
  `public/`, are never components.
- **Styles.** A top-level `<style>` is scoped to the file's content, like a top-level block in a
  `.stsx` file, and `<style global>` is not scoped. A `<style>` nested inside an element scopes to
  that element's subtree, as in `.stsx`. A `<style>` inside `<template>` (a web component's shadow
  DOM) or `<svg>` is left as it is. `$name` references are not available: there is no JS scope.
- **Scripts.** `<script>` and `<script type="module">` run as client modules: bundled by Vite and
  loaded in the browser wherever the component renders, the way an island's module is. Inline
  scripts and `src` files are both bundled. A relative `src` is resolved against the HTML file.
  Classic scripts become modules too, so they are deferred and strict. Scripts with other types
  (`application/ld+json`, `importmap`) stay in the markup.
- **Templates.** A `<template>`'s content stays verbatim, unscoped. So does the content of
  `<noscript>`. Comments and the doctype are dropped.
- **Attributes** are kept as written, including inline handlers (`onclick="…"`) and names JSX
  cannot write (`@click`, `x-on:click.prevent`), which are passed through a spread.
- **Asset URLs.** Relative URLs in `<img src>` and `srcset`, `<source src>` and `srcset`,
  `<video src>` and `poster`, `<audio src>`, `<track src>`, and `<a href>` to a file (an extension
  other than `.html` or `.md`) are bundled. They resolve against the `.md` or `.html` file, as
  `import url from "./photo.jpg?url"` does in a `.stsx` module: Vite serves them in dev and
  fingerprints them in builds (`/assets/photo-[hash].jpg`, or a data URL under its inline limit).
  Markdown images and links render as these elements, so their relative URLs are bundled too.
  Absolute paths (`/logo.svg`, from `public/`), URLs with a scheme or a query, fragments (`#top`)
  and links to pages (`./about`, `./next.md`) are kept as written. A missing file fails the
  build.

Raw `<style>` in Markdown follows the same rules. Raw `<script>` in Markdown is an error, with
the file and line ([LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md)); scripts belong in `.html` imports.

**How scripts load.** When a file has scripts, its component also renders an empty island with
`client:load`. On a server-rendered page, the island loader imports the island's module, which
imports the scripts, so they run once per page however many times the component renders. In a
client render, the scripts load with the component's module. An edit to such a file reloads the
page in dev, since scripts such as `customElements.define` cannot run twice.

> **Status:** available in `lumen dev` and builds, with HMR: an edit re-renders the content and
> hot-updates its CSS.

## API

| Import / option                                      | Gives                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumen({ md: true })`                                | Enables `.md` imports                                 |
| `lumen({ md: { frontmatter(data, { file }) {} } })`  | Enables them, with a build-time frontmatter hook      |
| `lumen({ html: true })`                              | Enables `.html` imports                               |
| `import Post, { frontmatter } from "./post.md"`      | `Post: () => JSX.Element`; `frontmatter: Frontmatter` |
| `import { headings } from "./post.md"`               | `ReadonlyArray<{ depth; text; id }>`, document order  |
| `declare module "*.md" { interface Frontmatter {} }` | Declares the fields your hook guarantees              |
| `import Card from "./card.html"`                     | `Card: () => JSX.Element`                             |
| `import.meta.glob("./posts/*.md", { eager: true })`  | Every post's module (component and frontmatter)       |

The types come with `lumen/env` (`"types": ["lumen/env"]` in `tsconfig.json`).

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts: Markdown with validated frontmatter, and HTML imports
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import lumen from "lumen/vite";
import * as z from "zod";

const Post = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  date: z.coerce.date(),
  draft: z.boolean().default(false),
});

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumen({ md: { frontmatter: (data) => Post.parse(data) }, html: true })],
});
```

```ts
// src/content.d.ts: the fields the hook guarantees, merged into lumen/env's `Frontmatter`
declare module "*.md" {
  interface Frontmatter {
    title: string;
    date: Date;
    draft: boolean;
  }
}
```

```stsx
// src/routes/blog/index.stsx: a list of posts and the latest one, with its table of contents
import type { Frontmatter, Heading } from "*.md";

type Post = {
  default: () => JSX.Element;
  frontmatter: Frontmatter;
  headings: ReadonlyArray<Heading>;
};
// `import.meta.glob` is Vite's (types from `vite/client`).
const posts = Object.values(import.meta.glob<Post>("../../posts/*.md", { eager: true })).toSorted(
  (a, b) => b.frontmatter.date.getTime() - a.frontmatter.date.getTime(),
);

export default function Blog() {
  const { default: Latest, headings } = posts[0]!;
  return (
    <main>
      <ul>
        {posts.map((post) => (
          <li>{post.frontmatter.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <nav aria-label="On this page">
        {headings
          .filter((heading) => heading.depth === 2)
          .map((heading) => (
            <a href={`#${heading.id}`}>{heading.text}</a>
          ))}
      </nav>
      <article class="post">
        <Latest />
      </article>
      <style>
        .post :deep(h2) { margin-top: 2rem; }
      </style>
    </main>
  );
}
```

```html
<!-- src/components/user-card.html: a web component in one file -->
<template id="user-card">
  <style>
    :host {
      display: block;
    }
  </style>
  <slot></slot>
</template>
<user-card>Ada Lovelace</user-card>
<script type="module">
  customElements.define(
    "user-card",
    class extends HTMLElement {
      connectedCallback() {
        const template = document.getElementById("user-card");
        this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" }).append(template.content.cloneNode(true));
      }
    },
  );
</script>
<style>
  user-card {
    margin-block: 1rem;
  }
</style>
```

The Markdown's elements belong to the post's component, so the route styles them with
`:deep()` under its own `.post` element. The web component's shadow styles stay in its template;
its light-DOM rule is scoped to the file.

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting the option.** `.md` and `.html` imports are off by default; without
  `lumen({ md: true })` Vite tries to read the file as JavaScript.
- **Trusting frontmatter types without a check.** `frontmatter` has `unknown` values. Declare
  fields in `Frontmatter` (as above) only when the hook validates the data.
- **Styling Markdown from a scoped block without `:deep()`.** The rendered elements belong to the
  Markdown component. Use `:deep()`, a class on a wrapper plus `:deep()`, or a `<style>` in the
  `.md` file itself.
- **Targeting `body` or `html` from an HTML file's `<style>`.** Its top-level styles are scoped
  to the file's content (`LUM3005`: the selector matches no element). Use `<style global>`.
- **A `<script>` in Markdown.** It fails with [LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md). Move the markup
  and script to an `.html` file and import that, or render the Markdown next to an island.
- **Expecting a script per use.** A file's scripts run once per page, not once per rendered
  component. Query the elements they work on (`document.querySelectorAll`) or use a custom
  element, which runs its code for every instance.
- **Linking to a file that is not there.** A relative asset URL (`<img src="./photo.jpg">`) is an import:
  a typo or a missing file fails the build. Files meant to be served as they are belong in
  `public/`, with an absolute URL (`/downloads/app.zip`).
- **Relative links between pages.** A Markdown link to `./next-post` is kept as written, so it resolves
  against the page's URL, not the file's. Link to the route's URL instead (`/blog/next-post`).

## Related diagnostics

The generated component compiles like a `.stsx` file, so style diagnostics apply to its blocks,
for example [LUM3005](../errors/LUM3005.md) for a selector that matches nothing.
[LUM1008](../errors/LUM1008.md) reports a `<script>` in a Markdown file. A frontmatter
block that is not a mapping, or a hook that throws, fails the build with the file's name.

See also: [Styles](styles.md), [Islands](islands.md), [SVG imports](svg.md), [reference: `lumen/vite`](../reference/vite.md), [reference: JSX types](../reference/jsx.md).

<!-- source: concepts/head.md -->

# Head and document

> Set head content with `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>` from any component. Lumen renders `<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>` for you; `src/document.stsx` customizes them.

## Concept

**Head components.** `<Title>`, `<Meta>` and `<Head>` can be used in any component, layout or page.
There is no `meta` export: these components are the one way to set head content.

- `<Title>`: the deepest one wins, so a page overrides its layouts.
- `<Meta name="…" content="…" />`: attributes as in HTML. Metas with the same `charset`, `name`,
  `property`, `http-equiv` or `itemprop` dedupe: the deepest one wins, and the previous value comes
  back when it is removed.
- `<Head>`: any other head elements (`<link>`, `<script>`). Elements already in `<head>` are not
  duplicated.

**On the server** they are collected while the shell renders and flushed into `<head>`. Inside a
streamed `<Suspense>` boundary they are too late (`LUM5004`). **In the browser** (islands, SPA)
they update `document.title` and `<head>` live, and are removed with their component.

**Document.** By default Lumen renders the HTML document. `src/document.stsx` takes over
`<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>`: it receives `{ head, body }` and must render each once. It renders
like any component, so it can set defaults with `<Title>`/`<Meta>` and provide context to pages.
`{props.head}` also carries the page's stylesheets, preload hints and island loader. `{props.body}`
is followed by the page's island records and its streamed `<Suspense>` content, so the whole page
stays inside `<body>` with either document.

> **Status:** available on the server (`renderToStream`) and in the browser; the default and custom
> documents are rendered by the request handler.

## API

| API                     | Use                                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<Title>{text}</Title>` | The document title; the deepest wins.                                               |
| `<Meta … />`            | A `<meta>` tag, keyed by `charset`, `name`, `property`, `http-equiv` or `itemprop`. |
| `<Head>…</Head>`        | Other head elements.                                                                |
| `DocumentProps`         | `{ head, body }`: props of `src/document.stsx`.                                     |

## Example

```stsx check file=document.stsx
// src/document.stsx
import { Meta, type DocumentProps } from "lumen";

export default function Document(props: DocumentProps) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
        <Meta name="description" content="A Lumen site" />
        {props.head}
      </head>
      <body>{props.body}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/about.tsx
// src/routes/about.tsx
import { Head, Meta, Title } from "lumen";

export default function About() {
  return (
    <main>
      <Title>About us</Title>
      <Meta name="description" content="Who we are" />
      <Head>
        <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/about" />
      </Head>
      <h1>About us</h1>
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **A `meta` or `title` export.** There is none; render `<Title>` and `<Meta>`.
- **`<Title>` inside `<Suspense>`** on a server route: the head was already sent (`LUM5004`). Set
  it in the page body outside the boundary.
- **Rendering `props.head` or `props.body` twice** in `document.stsx`. Render each exactly once.
- **Writing `<title>` or `<meta>` elements directly in a page.** They land in the body. Use the
  components.
- **Setting `document.title` in an effect.** It fights with `<Title>`; use the component.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM5004](../errors/LUM5004.md): head or status change inside a streamed boundary.

See also: [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [reference: components](../reference/components.md).

<!-- source: concepts/compiler.md -->

# Compiler and diagnostics

> A Rust compiler (OXC and Lightning CSS) turns `.stsx` and `.tsx` into fine-grained client code or string-concatenating server code. Every rule it enforces has a stable `LUMxxxx` code with a docs page.

## Concept

**Pipeline.** For each `.stsx`/`.tsx` module the Vite plugin calls the compiler, which:

1. **scans** the file for `<style>` blocks and masks them (replaces them with spaces, keeping every
   offset), so the rest is valid TSX;
2. parses and analyses the TSX: components, props, compiled idioms, `await` sites, islands and
   `$name` references;
3. compiles the CSS (scoping by placement, `$name` substitution, constant math folding, targets,
   minification);
4. generates JS for the **client** (cloned templates, bindings, delegated events) or the **server**
   (string concatenation with escaping), with source maps. Types are stripped.

Vite's own JSX transform is disabled for Lumen files, and `node_modules` is excluded.

**The masking invariant.** Masked TSX parses as valid TSX with identical offsets. Tools rely on it:
TypeScript type-checks _shadow files_ (`.lumen/shadow/<path>.stsx.tsx`, the masked text), so
errors map back to the same line and column of the `.stsx`. `$name` references stay in place as
real TS expressions (`$radius.lg` becomes `{radius.lg}` inside JSX, `;radius.lg;` at top level), so
TypeScript checks them too.

**Scanner rules.**

- `<style` must be followed by whitespace or `>`; it is recognised wherever a JSX element can
  start. Inside JSX text, quotes (as in `Don't`) do not start strings.
- The only attribute is `global`; content runs to the first `</style>`.
- A `<style>` inside `<svg>` is native SVG CSS: emitted verbatim and unscoped.

**Diagnostics.** Every diagnostic has the shape
`{ code, severity, message, span, labels, help, fix?, docs }`. Codes are stable forever and never
reused; the compiler's registry is the source of truth, and the [error pages](../errors/README.md)
are generated from it. They appear in the Vite overlay, in `lumen check`, in the editor and in
`--format json` output.

| Range | Area                                                                        |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1xxx  | File format: syntax, scanner, `<style>` blocks                              |
| 2xxx  | Reactivity: stale values, writes during render, early returns               |
| 3xxx  | Styles: placement, `$name` references, unused CSS                           |
| 4xxx  | Islands and boundaries: exports, serialization, server-only code, hydration |
| 5xxx  | Routing and server: route files, prerender, streaming                       |

**Tooling on top.** `lumen check` (typegen, shadow files, `tsc --noEmit`, scanner and compiler
diagnostics), `lumen lint` (oxlint on shadows, optional stylelint on blocks), `lumen fmt` (oxfmt
plus each block's CSS), and the language server (a TypeScript 7 LSP proxy plus CSS features in
blocks, the compiler's diagnostics as you type and each JSX expression's execution contract in
hovers) all share the one scanner. TypeScript plugins
are not used.

## API

| API                               | Use                                                  |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumen check [--format json]`     | Type-check and report diagnostics; exit 1 on errors. |
| `lumen explain <code>`            | Print a diagnostic's explanation.                    |
| `lumen docs <topic>`              | Print or search these docs.                          |
| `lumen/vite`                      | The plugin that runs the compiler in Vite.           |
| `.lumen/shadow/`, `.lumen/types/` | Generated shadow TSX and route types (git-ignored).  |

## Example

```stsx check
// The masked view TypeScript sees: the block becomes spaces, `$pad` stays as `{pad}`.
export function Box() {
  const pad = "1rem";
  return (
    <div class="box">
      Content
      <style>
        .box { padding: $pad; }
      </style>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```sh
$ lumen check --format json
{ "command": "check", "ok": true, "diagnostics": [], "summary": { "errors": 0, "warnings": 0, "hints": 0, "files": 0 } }
$ lumen explain LUM3010
```

## Common mistakes

- **Running bare `tsc` without shadow files.** `import "./X.stsx"` only resolves after shadows
  exist. Run `lumen check` (or `lumen typegen`), or keep the dev server or editor running.
- **A `tsconfig.json` that neither extends `.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json` nor sets `rootDirs`
  and `.lumen/shadow`.** `lumen check` reports the missing options (`LUM6001`); extend the
  generated file ([tsconfig](../reference/jsx.md#tsconfigjson)).
- **Importing `.stsx` across `src/` or from a workspace package with a standalone tsconfig.** Its
  `rootDirs` only pair `src`. Extend `.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json` instead
  ([tsconfig](../reference/jsx.md#imports-outside-src-and-stsx-from-other-packages)).
- **Ignoring a code because the message is short.** Run `lumen explain <code>` for the cause and
  the fix.
- **Expecting TypeScript plugins.** Lumen uses stock `tsc` and a language server; there is no TS
  plugin to configure.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM1001](../errors/LUM1001.md): syntax error.
- [LUM1002](../errors/LUM1002.md): unsupported by this compiler version.
- [LUM1003](../errors/LUM1003.md): scanner ambiguity.
- [All diagnostics](../errors/README.md).

See also: [Styles](styles.md), [reference: CLI](../reference/cli.md).

<!-- source: concepts/testing.md -->

# Testing

> Test components with Vitest through the Lumen Vite plugin: mount into a DOM environment, interact, call `flushSync()`, assert. Test server rendering with `renderToString`.

## Concept

Vitest uses your Vite config, so `lumen()` compiles `.stsx` and `.tsx` test subjects the same way
as the app. Two things matter for component tests:

- **A DOM environment.** Use `happy-dom` (or `jsdom`), per file with
  `// @vitest-environment happy-dom` or for all tests with `test.environment`.
- **The browser build of `lumen`.** `lumen` has a browser entry (signals, the DOM renderer) and a
  `node` entry (server rendering, where signals are plain values and effects never run). Vitest
  resolves Node conditions, but `lumen()` gives tests in a DOM environment the browser entry of
  `lumen`, so mounted components update. Tests without a DOM environment keep the `node` entry.

Updates are batched: after a write or an event outside a delegated handler, call `flushSync()`
before asserting. Delegated events (`onClick`) need the element to be attached to `document`.

Server rendering is tested with `renderToString(() => <Page />)` under the `node` entry: a test
file without a DOM environment, in the same project.

> **Status:** `@lumen/testing` (a `render()` helper and Testing Library integration) is planned.
> Until then, use `mount` from `lumen/dom` as shown here.

## API

| API                                                | Use                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `mount(() => <App />, container)` from `lumen/dom` | Render into a DOM node; returns a disposer. |
| `flushSync()`                                      | Run pending bindings and effects now.       |
| `renderToString(() => <App />)`                    | Server-render to a string (node entry).     |

## Example

```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import lumen from "lumen/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumen()],
  test: { environment: "happy-dom" },
});
```

```tsx check file=Counter.test.tsx
// src/Counter.test.tsx
import { flushSync } from "lumen";
import { mount } from "lumen/dom";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { Counter } from "./Counter.stsx";

it("counts clicks", () => {
  const container = document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"));
  const dispose = mount(() => <Counter start={2} />, container);

  const button = container.querySelector("button")!;
  button.click();
  flushSync();

  expect(button.textContent).toContain("Clicked 3 times");
  dispose();
  container.remove();
});
```

## Common mistakes

- **No DOM environment.** Without `happy-dom` (or `jsdom`) there is no `document`, and `lumen`
  resolves to its `node` entry, which has no reactive graph: set the environment for component
  tests.
- **Asserting right after a write.** Effects and bindings run in a microtask; call `flushSync()`
  first.
- **Clicking a detached element.** Delegated handlers listen at `document`; append the container
  to `document.body`.
- **Not disposing.** Call the disposer returned by `mount` so effects and listeners from one test
  do not leak into the next.
- **Testing server components in a DOM environment.** Async server components that use
  `request()`, `cookies()` or `*.server.ts` modules belong in server-side tests with
  `renderToString`.

## Related diagnostics

- [LUM4003](../errors/LUM4003.md): server-only module in a client graph (also `renderToString` called with the browser entry).
- [LUM4004](../errors/LUM4004.md): browser API at module scope.

See also: [Getting started](../getting-started.md), [reference: `lumen/dom`](../reference/dom.md), [reference: server](../reference/server.md).

<!-- source: concepts/security.md -->

# Security

> `lumen({ csp: "strict" })` sends a strict Content Security Policy: a fresh nonce on every inline script and style Lumen writes and on those you write in JSX, `cspNonce()` for markup you build yourself, and hashes for prerendered pages. Form actions are also checked against cross-site posts.

## Concept

**Strict Content Security Policy.** A strict CSP lets the browser run only the scripts and apply
only the styles the page meant to include, so injected markup cannot run code. With
`lumen({ csp: "strict" })`:

- **Pages rendered per request** (`server` routes, `spa` routes that reach the server) get a new
  random nonce for each response. Every inline `<script>` and `<style>` Lumen writes carries it:
  the page's stylesheets that are inlined (see [Styles](styles.md)), the island loader, the
  streamed `<Suspense>` swaps, the speculation rules, the View Transitions opt-in and module
  preloads. The response gets this header:

  ```
  Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'
  ```

  `'strict-dynamic'` lets the scripts the page loads import their own modules (islands, SPA
  routes). Stylesheets from your own origin are allowed; inline styles need the nonce.

- **Prerendered pages** (`static` routes, the shells of `spa` pages) are files that every visitor
  gets as they are, so a nonce would be the same for everyone. Each one gets the policy as
  `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">`, first in `<head>`, with the SHA-256 hash of each
  of its inline scripts and styles and `'self'` for scripts and stylesheets of your origin. It
  works on any static host.
- **`style` props** render as rules of a nonce'd (or hashed) `<style>` that target a `data-l-v`
  attribute, instead of `style="…"` attributes, which a strict policy refuses. In the browser,
  styles are set through the CSSOM, which the policy allows.
- **Your own inline scripts and styles** written in JSX get the nonce automatically: a
  `<script innerHTML={…}>` in the document, a JSON-LD block, an SVG `<style>`. An explicit `nonce`
  prop wins. Strings rendered as text are escaped and never become elements, and raw HTML strings
  (`innerHTML` of another element) never get a nonce. On prerendered pages the hash covers them.
- **Static `style="…"` strings** (in JSX, and in `.md`/`.html` imports) are applied like `style`
  props: a nonce'd rule on the server, the CSSOM in the browser.
- **`cspNonce()`** returns the response's nonce during a server render (the document included) and
  in middleware, and `undefined` without strict CSP or while prerendering. Use it for markup you
  build yourself: a third-party snippet as a string, a custom `Content-Security-Policy` header, a
  script you create at runtime. In the browser it reads `<meta property="csp-nonce">`.
- **Your own policy wins.** A `Content-Security-Policy` header from `lumen({ headers })` for the
  path, or one set with `response().setHeader()` or by middleware, replaces Lumen's; with `headers`,
  the path's prerendered pages get no `<meta>` policy either. `lumen dev` puts nonces on the page but sends no policy,
  because Vite injects styles of its own for hot updates.

Elements that the client creates later (a `<style>` inside an `<svg>` rendered after a client
navigation) take the nonce from `<meta property="csp-nonce">`. A prerendered page has no nonce,
so such an element is refused there unless it was in the prerendered HTML: put its rules in the
file's `<style>` block.

**Client navigation.** `navigate()` and the redirects of enhanced form actions only
follow `http:` and `https:` URLs (relative ones included); a `javascript:` or `data:` location
throws a `TypeError` instead of running in the page. Spread props drop lowercase `on*` keys
(`{...{ onclick: "…" }}`): an inline handler attribute is a script sink, so handlers are only
functions in `onClick`.

**Cross-site form posts.** Form actions and form-encoded posts to endpoints are checked against
the `Origin` header (on by default, `lumen({ csrf })`); see [Data and actions](data-and-actions.md).

## API

| Option / export                   | Meaning                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumen({ csp: "strict" })`        | Nonces per response, the policy header, hash policies for prerendered pages |
| `cspNonce(): string \| undefined` | The response's nonce (from `lumen`), for markup the app builds itself       |
| `<meta property="csp-nonce">`     | Written by Lumen with the nonce; the client's preload helper reads it       |

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumen from "lumen/vite";

export default { plugins: [lumen({ csp: "strict" })] };
```

```tsx
// src/document.tsx: an inline script that runs before the first paint
import type { DocumentProps } from "lumen";

const THEME = `document.documentElement.dataset.theme = localStorage.getItem("theme") ?? "auto"`;

export default function Document(props: DocumentProps) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8" />
        <script innerHTML={THEME} />
        {props.head}
      </head>
      <body>{props.body}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

On a server-rendered page Lumen gives the script the response's nonce; on a prerendered page the
page's policy lists the script's hash.

## Common mistakes

- **An inline script built as a string** (`<div innerHTML={'<script>…</script>'}>`, a snippet
  added at runtime). Lumen only nonces elements written in JSX: the browser refuses it and logs a
  CSP violation. Write it as a JSX `<script>`, add `nonce={cspNonce()}` to the markup you build,
  or load the code as a module.
- **A `<style>` inside an `<svg>` that only the client renders, on a prerendered page.** No nonce
  exists there. Put the rules in the file's `<style>` block.
- **Expecting the policy in `lumen dev`.** Dev sends none; check with `lumen build` and
  `lumen preview` or your server.
- **Adding `'unsafe-inline'` to make an error go away.** It disables the protection for every
  inline script. Find the element in the console message and give it the nonce instead.

## Related diagnostics

None yet: a violation shows in the browser console, with the refused element.

See also: [Head and document](head.md), [Styles](styles.md), [Rendering modes](rendering-modes.md), [reference: `lumen/vite`](../reference/vite.md), [reference: app APIs](../reference/app.md).

<!-- source: reference/reactivity.md -->

# `lumen`: reactivity

> Signatures and behavior of the reactive core exported by `lumen`: signals, computeds, effects, stores, owners, context and in-flight state.

All of these are exported by `lumen` in the browser and on the server. On the server (the `node`
entry) signals are plain cells, computeds evaluate once per request, and `effect`/`onMount` never
run. Concepts: [Signals and reactivity](../concepts/signals.md).

## signal

```ts
function signal<T>(value: T, options?: SignalOptions<T>): Signal<T>;

interface Signal<T> {
  (): T; // read (tracked)
  set(value: T): void;
  update(fn: (value: T) => T): void;
  peek(): T; // read without tracking
}
interface SignalOptions<T> {
  /** When a write counts as a change. Default Object.is; false: every write is a change. */
  equals?: false | ((a: T, b: T) => boolean);
```
