```ts
}
```

## computed

```ts
function computed<T>(fn: (previous: T | undefined) => T, options?: SignalOptions<T>): Computed<T>;
type Computed<T> = () => T;
```

Lazy (runs on first read), cached, glitch-free. `fn` must be pure: no signal writes (`LUM2002`).
An unobserved computed unlinks itself from its sources.

## effect

```ts
function effect(fn: EffectFn): () => void;
type EffectFn = () => void | (() => void);
```

Runs `fn` after the DOM updates, then again whenever a signal it read changes. A returned function
is a cleanup, run before the next run and on disposal. Returns a disposer. Owned by the current
owner, so it is disposed with the component.

## onMount

```ts
function onMount(fn: EffectFn): void;
```

Runs `fn` once, untracked, after the current owner's DOM is mounted. It may return a cleanup.

## onCleanup

```ts
function onCleanup(fn: () => void): void;
```

Registers `fn` on the current owner: it runs when the owner is disposed (or, for an effect, before
its next run).

## lifetime

```ts
function lifetime(): AbortSignal;
```

An `AbortSignal` for the current owner. Aborted when the owner is disposed, when an effect re-runs,
or when an async component run is superseded. On the server it is the request's signal. Throws
outside an owner.

## untrack

```ts
function untrack<T>(fn: () => T): T;
```

Runs `fn` without subscribing the current scope to the signals it reads.

## batch

```ts
function batch<T>(fn: () => T): T;
```

Defers dependents until `fn` returns, so they run once. Delegated event handlers are batched
automatically.

## flushSync

```ts
function flushSync(): void;
```

Runs pending computeds, DOM bindings and effects now, instead of in the next microtask.

## store

```ts
function store<T extends object>(value: T): T;
```

Wraps a plain object or array in a deep reactive proxy: reads track per property, writes notify
only on change, array methods work. Class instances, `Map`s, `Set`s and frozen objects are returned
as is.

## snapshot

```ts
function snapshot<T>(value: T): T;
```

A deep plain copy of a store, of a value inside one (`snapshot(state.items)`), or of plain data
that holds stores. Plain objects and arrays are copied; other values (`Date`s, `Map`s, class
instances) are kept as they are, and shared or circular references stay shared. Use it where a
proxy does not work: `structuredClone()` and `postMessage()` (to a worker or an AudioWorklet)
throw on proxies, and a copy does not change when the store does (saving, undo history). Reads
are not tracked: in an effect, read the properties it should react to. On the server it copies the
plain object.

```ts
const song = store({ title: "Demo", rows: [] as number[][] });
worker.postMessage({ type: "song", song: snapshot(song) });
```

## createContext, provide, inject

```ts
function createContext<T>(defaultValue: T): Context<T>;
function createContext<T>(): Context<T | undefined>;
function provide<T>(context: Context<T>, value: T): void;
function inject<T>(context: Context<T>): T;
interface Context<T> {
  readonly id: symbol;
  readonly defaultValue: T;
}
```

`provide` sets a value on the current owner for everything created below it; `inject` returns the
nearest provided value, or the default. Context survives `await` in async components.

## pending

```ts
function pending(): boolean;
```

Inside an async component (its body or its UI): whether a **re-run** is in flight. The first load is
not a re-run (`<Suspense>` covers it). Reading it in the body does not re-run the component.
Always `false` on the server.

## busy

```ts
function busy(): boolean;
```

App-wide: whether anything is in flight: an async component run, a `<Suspense>` showing its
fallback, a form submission (`submit()`) or an SPA navigation. Reactive. Always `false` on the
server.

## resource

```ts
function resource<T>(fetcher: (signal: AbortSignal) => T | PromiseLike<T>): Resource<T>;

interface Resource<T> {
  (): T | undefined; // latest value, tracked
  loading(): boolean;
  error(): unknown;
  refetch(): void; // aborts a load in flight and loads again
}
```

Low-level on-demand loading. `fetcher` runs now and whenever a signal it read synchronously
changes; its `AbortSignal` aborts when superseded or disposed. The first load counts as pending
for the nearest `<Suspense>`. Errors are not thrown: read `error()`. Browser only: on the server it
stays loading. Prefer [async components](../concepts/async.md).

## Example

```tsx check
import { batch, effect, lifetime, onCleanup, resource, signal, untrack } from "lumen";

export function Clock() {
  const now = signal(new Date());
  const timer = setInterval(() => now.set(new Date()), 1000);
  onCleanup(() => clearInterval(timer));

  const first = signal("Ada");
  const last = signal("Lovelace");
  const rename = () =>
    batch(() => {
      first.set("Grace");
      last.set("Hopper");
    });

  effect(() => {
    console.log(`${first()} ${last()} at`, untrack(now).toISOString());
  });

  const user = resource((signal) =>
    fetch(`/api/users/${first()}`, { signal }).then((res) => res.json() as Promise<{ id: string }>),
  );

  return (
    <p onClick={rename}>
      {now().toLocaleTimeString()} · {user.loading() ? "…" : user()?.id}
      {String(lifetime().aborted)}
    </p>
  );
}
```

<!-- source: reference/components.md -->

# `lumen`: components

> Signatures and behavior of the built-in components and element helpers exported by `lumen`: `Suspense`, `ErrorBoundary`, `Portal`, `Dynamic`, `ref`, `Head`, `Title` and `Meta`.

All are exported by `lumen` in the browser and on the server. Concepts:
[Components](../concepts/components.md), [Async components](../concepts/async.md),
[Head and document](../concepts/head.md).

## Suspense

```ts
function Suspense(props: SuspenseProps): JSX.Element;
interface SuspenseProps {
  /** Shown while new content below is pending. */
  fallback?: JSX.Element;
  children?: JSX.Element;
}
```

Shows `fallback` while **new** async content below it is pending: the first load, and async
components or resources that a branch mounts later. Re-runs of revealed content keep their stale UI
(`pending()` tells them apart). Hidden content stays alive. A shown fallback counts for `busy()`.
On the server, a boundary marks content that streams after the shell; with prerendering it is
resolved inline.

## ErrorBoundary

```ts
function ErrorBoundary(props: ErrorBoundaryProps): JSX.Element;
interface ErrorBoundaryProps {
  /** Rendered instead of the children after an error. */
  fallback?: JSX.Element | ((error: unknown, retry: () => void) => JSX.Element);
  children?: JSX.Element;
}
```

Renders `fallback` when its children throw while rendering, an effect below throws, or an async
component below rejects. `retry()` disposes the fallback and mounts the children again. On the
server, an error in a streamed boundary renders the nearest `ErrorBoundary` in place.

## Portal

```ts
function Portal(props: PortalProps): JSX.Element;
interface PortalProps {
  /** Where the content goes. Default: document.body. */
  mount?: Node;
  children?: JSX.Element;
}
```

Renders `children` into a `<div>` appended to `mount`, removed with the owner. Delegated events
from the portal's content continue at the portal's position in the component tree.

## Dynamic

```ts
function Dynamic(props: DynamicProps): JSX.Element;
interface DynamicProps {
  /** A component or an intrinsic tag name. Nothing renders while it is nullish or false. */
  component: Component | string | null | undefined | false;
  [prop: string]: unknown;
}
```

Renders `component` with the other props, re-creating it only when `component` changes.

## ref

```ts
function ref<T extends Element>(): JSX.Ref<T>;
```

A callback for the `ref` prop that can also be read like a signal: `input()` is `undefined` until
the element exists. Pass it as `ref={input}`.

## Title

```ts
function Title(props: { children?: JSX.Element }): JSX.Element;
```

Sets the document title. The deepest `<Title>` wins, so a page overrides its layouts.

## Meta

```ts
function Meta(props: Record<string, unknown>): JSX.Element;
```

Adds or updates a `<meta>` in `<head>`, with the given attributes. Metas with the same `charset`,
`name`, `property`, `http-equiv` or `itemprop` dedupe: the deepest wins, and the previous one comes
back when it is removed.

## Head

```ts
function Head(props: { children?: JSX.Element }): JSX.Element;
```

Appends its children to `<head>` and removes them on disposal. Elements equal to one already in
`<head>` (for example rendered by the server) are skipped.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Dynamic, ErrorBoundary, Portal, Suspense, ref, signal } from "lumen";

function Info() {
  return <p>Info</p>;
}

export function Dialog() {
  const open = signal(false);
  const kind = signal<"h2" | "h3">("h2");
  const button = ref<HTMLButtonElement>();

  return (
    <ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, retry) => <button onClick={retry}>{String(error)}</button>}>
      <button ref={button} onClick={() => open.set(true)}>
        Open
      </button>
      {open() && (
        <Portal>
          <div role="dialog">
            <Dynamic component={kind()}>Title</Dynamic>
            <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
              <Dynamic component={Info} />
            </Suspense>
            <button onClick={() => (open.set(false), button()?.focus())}>Close</button>
          </div>
        </Portal>
      )}
    </ErrorBoundary>
  );
}
```

<!-- source: reference/app.md -->

# `lumen`: app layer

> Signatures of the app-layer exports of `lumen`: data fetching, form actions, routing helpers, control flow, request APIs, cookies, env and the request-context types.

`lumen` exposes the same names in the browser and on the server. Server-only APIs exist in the
browser build as stubs that throw `LUM4003` with a hint; browser-only APIs reject on the server.
Concepts: [Data and actions](../concepts/data-and-actions.md), [Server](../concepts/server.md),
[Routing](../concepts/routing.md).

## Data

### fetchJSON

```ts
function fetchJSON<T = unknown>(input: string | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T>;
```

Fetches and parses JSON (`Accept: application/json` unless `init` sets it); an empty body is
`undefined`. Non-2xx responses throw a `FetchError`. During SSR, same-origin URLs are served
in-process through the request handler, with the page request's cookies and headers. Returns plain
data, so awaited results stay serializable in islands.

### FetchError, isFetchError

```ts
interface FetchError extends HttpError {
  readonly status: number; // 0 for network failures
  readonly url: string;
  /** Parsed JSON body for JSON responses, else text; undefined when empty. */
  readonly data: unknown;
}
function isFetchError(value: unknown): value is FetchError;
```

Thrown by `fetchJSON()` and by `submit()` for unexpected errors. An `HttpError`, so if a server
component lets it escape, the page renders `_error` (or `_404`) with the same status.

## Form actions

### submit

```ts
function submit(target: SubmitTarget, options?: SubmitOptions): Promise<ActionResult>;
// Typed by the action it posts to: submit<typeof actions.save>(event)
function submit<A extends ActionsExport>(
  target: SubmitTarget,
  options?: SubmitOptions,
): Promise<ActionResult<ActionSuccessData<A>, ActionFailureData<A>>>;

type SubmitTarget =
  | HTMLFormElement
  | Event // a submit event: onSubmit={submit}
  | FormData
  | URLSearchParams
  | Record<string, string | Blob | readonly (string | Blob)[]>;

interface SubmitOptions {
  /** A URL, or "?/name" for a named action. Default: the submitter's formaction, else the
   *  form's action, else the current URL. */
  action?: string;
  /** Default POST. A form must say method="post". */
  method?: string;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  /** Client-routed (SPA) pages: after a success, refresh the page's data with invalidate().
   *  Default true. MPA pages never invalidate on their own. */
  invalidate?: boolean;
}

type ActionResult<Data = unknown, Failure = unknown> =
  | { type: "success"; status: number; data: Data }
  | { type: "failure"; status: number; data: Failure }
  | { type: "redirect"; status: number; location: string };
```

Posts without a page load. `success` and `failure` set `actionData()`; `redirect` navigates.
On client-routed (SPA) pages, after a `success`, `submit()` runs [`invalidate()`](#invalidate) and
resolves once the page's data is fresh (decision-20); `{ invalidate: false }` skips it. On MPA pages
it never reloads: the island updates itself from the result, or calls `invalidate()` explicitly.
Failures, redirects and errors do not invalidate. Rejects only for unexpected errors (the action throws, an error response, a network
failure) with a `FetchError`, and with a `TypeError` for a redirect to a URL that is not `http(s)`
(a `javascript:` location never runs). Browser only: rejects on the server.

### submitting

```ts
function submitting(name?: string): boolean;
```

Whether a `submit()` is in flight; with a name, one to that named action (`?/name`). Reactive.
`false` on the server.

### actionData

```ts
function actionData(): unknown;
// Typed by the page's actions: actionData<typeof actions>() or actionData<typeof action>()
function actionData<A extends ActionsExport>(): ActionData<A> | undefined;
type ActionData<A extends ActionsExport> =
  | ActionSuccessData<A> // what the actions return (not fail() or a Response); void → undefined
  | ActionFailureData<A>; // the data they pass to fail()
// typeof action, typeof actions or typeof actions.name
type ActionsExport =
  | ((ctx: never) => unknown)
  | { readonly [name: string]: (ctx: never) => unknown };
```

The data of the last action result: what the action returned, or its `fail()` data. The type
argument is the actions export itself, never a data type: the result types are inferred from it.
`ActionData<typeof actions>` names the same type, for the props of a component that receives it
(`failed: ActionData<typeof action> | undefined`). Success and failure data are told apart by
their shape, as with React Router's `useActionData` and SvelteKit's `form`. Reactive in
the browser; after a no-JS form post it starts with the data the page was rendered with. On the
server: the current request's action result while the page re-renders after a post.

### fail, ActionFailure

```ts
function fail(status: number): ActionFailure<undefined>;
function fail<Data>(status: number, data: Data): ActionFailure<Data>;
```

A failed action result, usually for validation errors: `return fail(400, { errors })`. Without
JavaScript the page re-renders with `status`; `submit()` resolves with `{ type: "failure" }`.

### invalidate

```ts
function invalidate(): Promise<void>;
```

Refreshes the current page's server data after a mutation: re-runs the page's async components in
SPA routes (their UI stays until the new data arrives), reloads the page otherwise. A successful
`submit()` calls it for you on SPA pages only; on MPA pages call it yourself when the page needs
fresh server HTML. Browser only.

## Routing

### href

```ts
function href<P extends Routes>(pattern: P, ...args: HrefArgs<P>): string;
```

Builds a path from a route pattern, encoding each param; `params` is required when the pattern has
params. A `[...rest]` param keeps its `/` separators and may be empty. Throws on a missing or empty
`[param]`.

The path is below Vite's `base` and follows `lumen({ trailingSlash })`, on the server and in the
browser alike (`lumen dev`, `lumen build` and prerendering):

| `base`  | `trailingSlash` | `href("/")` | `href("/blog/[slug]", { slug: "a" })` | `href("/feed.xml")` |
| ------- | --------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `/`     | `"ignore"`      | `/`         | `/blog/a`                             | `/feed.xml`         |
| `/sub/` | `"never"`       | `/sub/`     | `/sub/blog/a`                         | `/sub/feed.xml`     |
| `/sub/` | `"always"`      | `/sub/`     | `/sub/blog/a/`                        | `/sub/feed.xml`     |

With `"always"`, a pattern whose last segment has a dot (an endpoint such as `/feed.xml`) gets no
trailing slash. A relative `base` (`./`) counts as `/`. Outside Vite (plain Node) the path is
root-relative.

### Route types

```ts
interface RouteMap {}                  // augmented by .lumen/types/routes.d.ts (typegen)
interface LayoutMap {}                 // the same, for layouts (by the URL scope of their folder)
type Routes = /* every route pattern, or string before typegen */;
type RouteParams<P extends Routes>;    // { slug: string } for "/blog/[slug]"
interface PageProps<P extends /* a page pattern */> { params: RouteParams<P> }
interface LayoutProps<P extends /* a layout pattern */> {
  params: /* the params of the layout's scope */;
  children: JSX.Element;
}
```

## Control flow

```ts
function redirect(location: string | URL, status?: 301 | 302 | 303 | 307 | 308): never;
function notFound(message?: string): never;
function error(status: number, message?: string): never; // 400-599
function isRedirect(value: unknown): value is Redirect;
function isHttpError(value: unknown): value is HttpError;
```

They throw; the framework renders a redirect, the nearest `_404` (404) or the nearest `_error`.
Without a status, `redirect()` uses 302 for GET/HEAD and 303 otherwise. `HttpError` is an `Error`
with a `status`.

## Request APIs (server)

```ts
function request(): Request;
function url(): URL;
function params<P extends Routes = never>(): RouteParams<P>; // Record<string, string> without P
function route(): Routes | undefined; // the matched pattern, "/blog/[slug]"; undefined if none
function locals(): Locals;
function cookies(): Cookies;
function response(): ResponseContext;
function env(name: string): string | undefined;
function publicEnv(source?: ServerEnv): Record<string, string>;
function cspNonce(): string | undefined; // lumen({ csp: "strict" }): the response's nonce
```

`cspNonce()` is `undefined` without strict CSP, outside a request and while prerendering (the
page's hash policy covers its inline elements); in the browser it reads
`<meta property="csp-nonce">`. See [Security](../concepts/security.md).

Available anywhere during a server render (also after `await`), scoped to the current request. In
the browser they throw `LUM4003`. `env()` reads the adapter's env, else `process.env`;
`publicEnv()` returns the `PUBLIC_*` subset.

```ts
interface ResponseContext {
  readonly status: number;
  setStatus(status: number): void;
  getHeader(name: string): string | null;
  setHeader(name: string, value: string): void;
}
```

Writable until the shell is sent; later writes throw `LUM5004`.

## Cookies

```ts
interface Cookies {
  get(name: string): string | undefined;
  getAll(): Array<{ name: string; value: string }>;
  set(name: string, value: string, options?: CookieOptions): void;
  delete(name: string, options?: CookieDeleteOptions): void;
}
interface CookieOptions {
  path?: string; // default "/"
  domain?: string;
  maxAge?: number; // seconds
  expires?: Date;
  httpOnly?: boolean; // default true
  secure?: boolean; // default: true in production and on https
  sameSite?: "lax" | "strict" | "none"; // default "lax"; "none" forces secure
  partitioned?: boolean; // CHIPS; forces secure
}
type CookieDeleteOptions = Pick<CookieOptions, "path" | "domain" | "secure" | "sameSite">;

function signedCookie(name: string, options?: SignedCookieOptions): SignedCookie;
interface SignedCookieOptions extends CookieOptions {
  /** HMAC secret; an array rotates keys (the first signs). Default: env LUMEN_SECRET. */
  secret?: string | readonly string[];
}
interface SignedCookie {
  readonly name: string;
  get(cookies: Cookies): Promise<string | undefined>; // undefined when the signature is invalid
  set(cookies: Cookies, value: string, options?: CookieOptions): Promise<void>;
  delete(cookies: Cookies, options?: CookieDeleteOptions): void;
}
```

## Context types

```ts
// P is a route pattern ("/books/[isbn]"); without one, params is Record<string, string>.
interface RequestContext<P extends Routes = never> {
  request: Request;
  url: URL;
  params: RouteParams<P>;
  locals: Locals;
  cookies: Cookies;
  env: ServerEnv; // Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>
}
interface ActionContext<P extends /* a page pattern */ = never> extends RequestContext<P> {
  formData(): Promise<FormData>; // parsed once; 400 if the body is not a form
}
type Middleware = (
  ctx: RequestContext,
  next: () => Promise<Response>,
) => Response | Promise<Response>;
type Endpoint<P extends /* an endpoint pattern */ = never> = (
  ctx: RequestContext<P>,
) => Response | Promise<Response>;
// Annotating with Action hides the result from actionData<typeof action>(): type the parameter
// with ActionContext<P> instead, or use `satisfies Action<P>`.
type Action<P extends /* a page pattern */ = never, Result = unknown> = (
  ctx: ActionContext<P>,
) => Result | Promise<Result>;
type HttpMethod = "GET" | "HEAD" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE" | "OPTIONS";
interface ErrorPageProps {
  status: number;
  error: Error & { status?: number };
}
interface DocumentProps {
  head: JSX.Element;
  body: JSX.Element;
}
interface Locals {} // augment: declare module "lumen" { interface Locals { … } }
```

## Example

```ts check file=routes/api/session.ts
// src/routes/api/session.ts
import { isHttpError, type Endpoint } from "lumen";

// Per request: it reads cookies and accepts POST, so it cannot be prerendered (LUM5005).
export const mode = "server";

export const GET: Endpoint<"/api/session"> = ({ cookies }) =>
  Response.json({ theme: cookies.get("theme") ?? "light" });

export const POST: Endpoint<"/api/session"> = async ({ request, cookies }) => {
  try {
    const { theme } = (await request.json()) as { theme: string };
    cookies.set("theme", theme, { maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 });
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (isHttpError(error)) throw error;
    return Response.json({ error: "Invalid JSON" }, { status: 400 });
  }
};
```

<!-- source: reference/server.md -->

# `lumen`: server rendering

> `renderToStream` and `renderToString` render components to HTML under the `node` entry of `lumen`; `lumen/server` is the server half of the compiler-runtime contract.

Most apps never call these directly: the request handler (and `lumen dev` / `lumen build`) does.
Use them for custom servers, tests and tools. Concepts:
[Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md).

## renderToStream

```ts
function renderToStream(
  root: () => unknown,
  options?: RenderToStreamOptions,
): Promise<RenderedShell>;

interface RenderToStreamOptions {
  /** Aborts the render: rejects a pending shell, ends the stream and aborts lifetime(). */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  /** SSG/prerender: render every Suspense boundary into the shell; no fallbacks, no stream. */
  resolveAll?: boolean;
  /** CSP nonce for the $swap scripts and strict-mode <style> rules. */
  nonce?: string;
  /** CSP strict mode: style props become nonce'd <style> rules. */
  strictStyles?: boolean;
  /** Maps an island module specifier to its URL for modulepreload hints. */
  islandUrl?: (specifier: string) => string;
  /**
   * URL of the island loader (lumen/dom/loader). A page with islands gets it once, as
   * <script type="module" async>: in `head` when the shell has islands, else in the first
   * streamed chunk with island records. Default: none (islands render but do not hydrate).
   */
  loaderUrl?: string;
  /** Errors of streamed boundaries that no ErrorBoundary handled. Default: console.error. */
  onError?: (error: unknown) => void;
}

interface RenderedShell {
  /** Collected <Title>/<Meta>/<Head> HTML, modulepreload hints and strict-mode styles. */
  head: string;
  /** The shell HTML, followed by the shell's island records. */
  body: string;
  /** Streamed boundary chunks to append inside <body>; null when nothing is pending. */
  stream: ReadableStream<string> | null;
}
```

Renders `root` shell-first (decision-19): resolves once everything outside `<Suspense>` is ready,
and rejects with the first error thrown while rendering the shell (so the caller can render an
error page with the right status). The stream then delivers each boundary as it resolves, out of
order.

## renderToString

```ts
function renderToString(
  root: () => unknown,
  options?: Omit<RenderToStreamOptions, "resolveAll">,
): Promise<string>;
```

Renders everything resolved (no fallbacks, no stream) and returns the body HTML. Used for
prerendering and tests.

Both are server-only: in the browser build of `lumen` they throw `LUM4003`.

## `lumen/server`

The server runtime that compiled server code imports (`ssr`, `escape`, `insert`, `list`, `branch`,
`branchArm`, `createComponent`, `island`, `$await`, …). It is the compiler-runtime contract, not an
application API: its members may change between versions without notice. It also re-exports
`renderToStream` and `renderToString`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { renderToStream } from "lumen";

function App() {
  return <h1>Hello</h1>;
}

export async function handle(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const { head, body, stream } = await renderToStream(() => <App />, { signal: request.signal });
  const encoder = new TextEncoderStream();
  const writer = encoder.writable.getWriter();
  void (async () => {
    await writer.write(`<!doctype html><html><head>${head}</head><body>${body}`);
    if (stream) for await (const chunk of stream) await writer.write(chunk);
    await writer.write("</body></html>");
    await writer.close();
  })();
  return new Response(encoder.readable, {
    headers: { "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" },
  });
}
```

<!-- source: reference/dom.md -->

# `lumen/dom`

> `mount` renders a component tree into a DOM element. The rest of `lumen/dom` is the client half of the compiler-runtime contract that compiled code imports.

## mount

```ts
function mount(code: () => JSX.Element, container: Element): () => void;
```

Renders `code()` into `container` (appended after its existing content) under a new root owner, and
marks the container as a delegation boundary. Returns a disposer that disposes the owner and
removes the rendered nodes. With the Vite plugin, an entry module that imports `mount` re-mounts on
hot updates.

## Compiler-runtime contract

`template`, `bind`, `insert`, `insertText`, `branch`, `list`, `selector`, `createComponent`, `mergeProps`,
`restProps`, `spread`, `delegateEvents`, `listen`, `attach`, `bindValue`, `bindChecked`,
`useRef`, `$async`, `$await`, `$leave` and friends are what the compiler emits calls to. They are
not an application API and may change between versions; write JSX instead.

## `lumen/dom/hydrate`

```ts
function hydrate<P extends object>(
  component: Component<P>,
  props: P,
  start: Node,
  end: Node,
  awaits?: Record<string, unknown>,
  slots?: readonly string[],
  fresh?: boolean,
): () => void;
```

Hydrates the server-rendered range between the comments `start` and `end` (an island's
`<!--l:ID-->` and `<!--/l:ID-->`): it renders `component` with `props`, and the compiled code
claims the server's nodes instead of creating new ones, so element identity, focus and text
selections survive. Returns a disposer.

- **Awaits are replayed.** `awaits` maps each first-run `await` of an async component to the value
  the server recorded (`"instancePath:site:occurrence"` keys), so hydration does not fetch again.
  The awaited expression still runs for tracking, with its fetch held off: when a signal it reads
  changes later, the component re-runs and fetches as usual.
- **Slots** (`slots`, the names of children and JSX props) become props holding the server's HTML:
  the nodes rendered inline (`<!--l:s:NAME-->…<!--/l:s-->`) are adopted where the island renders
  the slot; a slot the server did not render comes from its `<template data-l-slot="NAME">` when
  the island renders it later.
- **Mismatch.** When the client renders a different structure than the server's (another branch,
  element or list length), the island is disposed, its range cleared and rendered on the client;
  in dev, [LUM4006](../errors/LUM4006.md) is logged. A missing await record makes the client await
  again (also LUM4006 in dev).
- `fresh` (`client:only`) renders on the client without claiming.

Importing `lumen/dom/hydrate` also installs the hydration cursor that the compiled walk uses. Only
the island loader and hydrating entries import it; bundles that never hydrate do not include it.

## `lumen/dom/loader`

The island loader: a client entry, with no exports, that `lumen dev` and `lumen build` add to every
page that renders an island (`<script type="module" async>`, see [Islands](../concepts/islands.md));
with your own server, pass its URL as `renderToStream(root, { loaderUrl })`. It imports the app's
island manifest (`virtual:lumen/islands`, from `lumen/vite`), and:

- reads the island records (`<script type="application/json" data-l-islands>`) as each streamed
  chunk arrives, and finds each island's range;
- arms its trigger: `client:load` and `client:only` at once, `client:idle` on
  `requestIdleCallback`, `client:visible` when the range's first element intersects the viewport
  (the value is the `rootMargin`), `client:media` when the query matches;
- waits for an island whose range still holds a streamed `<Suspense>` fallback until its content
  (and the await records sent with it) arrives;
- imports the island's module and calls `hydrate()`;
- catches `click`, `input`, `submit` and `keydown` on an island that is not hydrated yet: it
  hydrates that island at once and dispatches the events again on their targets afterwards (an
  `input` restores the value typed meanwhile).

Islands inside slots that an island inserts later are hydrated when they appear.

## Example

```tsx check
import { signal } from "lumen";
import { mount } from "lumen/dom";

function App() {
  const name = signal("world");
  return <input bind:value={name} placeholder={`Hello, ${name()}`} />;
}

mount(() => <App />, document.getElementById("app")!);
```

<!-- source: reference/router.md -->

# `lumen/router`

> The client router for `spa` routes, built on the Navigation API: `<Link>`, `navigate()`, reactive `params()`, `route()`, `search()`, `url()` and `navigating()`, persistent layouts, transitions that hold the old page, scroll and focus restoration, and a client-side `_404`.

`lumen/router` works inside `spa` routes (`export const mode = "spa"`, or `lumen({ mode: "spa" })`
for the whole project); `<Link>` works on MPA pages too (see [Link](#link)). Pages and layouts of an SPA import it like any module; on the server
(`ssr` pages) the same names read the request: `params()`, `route()`, `url()` and `search()` return the
request's values, `<Link>` renders its `<a>`, `navigating()` is `false`, and `navigate()` and
`search.set()` throw (call them from event handlers and effects). Concepts:
[Routing](../concepts/routing.md), [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md).

## Components

### Link

```ts
function Link(props: LinkProps): JSX.Element;

type LinkProps = Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["a"], "href" | "children"> & {
  href: string;
  /** Default "hover" in spa pages; on MPA pages, lumen({ prefetch }). */
  prefetch?: "hover" | "viewport" | "none";
  children?: JSX.Element;
};
```

An `<a href>` with every attribute and event of `<a>`. The router navigates plain `<a>` links too;
`<Link>` adds:

- **Prefetch.** It loads the target route's modules ahead of the click: when the pointer enters
  the link or it gets focus (`hover`), when it enters the viewport (`viewport`), or not (`none`).
  Data still loads when the page renders. `spa` pages get no speculation rules, so this is the
  prefetch of their links.
- **On MPA pages** (static and server routes) there is no router: `<Link>` renders a plain `<a>`,
  outside islands without any JavaScript, and `prefetch` sets how the page's speculation rules from
  `lumen({ prefetch })` treat it ([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)). The `<a>` gets
  `data-l-prefetch="<level>"`; the rules skip `none` links, prefetch `viewport` links with `eager`
  and `hover` links with `moderate` eagerness, and give unmarked links (`<Link>` without
  `prefetch`, plain `<a>`) the project default. With `lumen({ prefetch: "none" })`, only pages that
  have `hover` or `viewport` links get rules. Browsers prefetch URLs: a `none` link to a URL that
  another link on the page prefetches does not stop it.
- **`aria-current="page"`** while its path is the current URL's path (style it with
  `a[aria-current="page"]`).

Build `href` with [`href()`](app.md#href) so the route and its params type-check.

## Navigation

### navigate

```ts
function navigate(href: string | URL, options?: NavigateOptions): Promise<void>;

interface NavigateOptions {
  /** Replace the current history entry instead of adding one. */
  replace?: boolean;
}
```

Navigates on the client when `href` belongs to the current SPA, else loads the document. Resolves
once the new page is on screen (its async content ready), or when another navigation supersedes
it. Browser only. Only `http:` and `https:` URLs (relative ones included) navigate: any other
scheme, such as `javascript:`, throws a `TypeError`.

### navigating

```ts
function navigating(): boolean;
```

Whether a navigation is in flight: from the click until the new page is on screen. Reactive, and
counted by [`busy()`](reactivity.md) (decision-20).

## Route state

### params

```ts
function params<P extends Routes = never>(): RouteParams<P>; // untyped: Record<string, string>
```

The current route's params, reactive: `params<"/songs/[id]">().id`. Pages also receive them as
`props.params`.

### route

```ts
function route(): Routes | undefined;
```

The matched route pattern, reactive: `route() === "/songs/[id]"`. Compare patterns instead of
matching `url().pathname`; typegen makes an unknown pattern a type error. `undefined` on a `_404`
page for an unknown URL (a matched route that throws `notFound()` keeps its pattern).

### url

```ts
function url(): URL;
```

The current URL, reactive. Do not mutate it.

### search

```ts
interface Search {
  (): URLSearchParams;
  set(
    next: SearchInit | ((current: URLSearchParams) => SearchInit),
    options?: NavigateOptions,
  ): Promise<void>;
}
const search: Search;

type SearchInit =
  | URLSearchParams
  | string
  | Record<string, string | number | boolean | readonly string[] | null | undefined>;
```

`search()` is the current URL's query, reactive (a new object per change). `search.set()`
navigates to the current path with a new query, keeping the scroll position; `null` and
`undefined` values are left out. It adds a history entry unless `{ replace: true }`.

While a page is still loading during a navigation, `params()`, `route()`, `url()` and `search()` called in it
(and its props) already describe the page it is loading; everything else keeps the shown URL until
the new page is on screen.

## Behaviour

- **Interception.** The router handles same-document navigations to URLs of its SPA: link clicks,
  `navigate()`, back/forward and (with the Navigation API) `GET` form submissions. URLs of other
  routes (`static` or `server` pages, endpoints, other SPAs) load the document. Without the
  Navigation API, a History API fallback intercepts link clicks and `popstate`; it is a chunk of its
  own that only those browsers load, shortly after the SPA starts (a click before it loads is a
  document navigation).
- **Persistent layouts.** A layout's `children` is the outlet. Layouts the old and the new page
  share stay mounted with their state; the first level that differs (another file, or other
  values of the params in its path, such as `songs/[id].stsx` for another song) is replaced. A
  navigation that only changes the query keeps every level and updates `search()`.
- **Transitions.** The new page is created off-screen. The old page stays until the new page's
  async content (async components and resources outside a `<Suspense>` of the new page) is ready;
  then the URL signals change and the pages swap in one step. A `<Suspense>` inside the new page
  shows its fallback instead.
- **Scroll and focus.** After a navigation the page scrolls to the top (or to the URL's `#hash`)
  and focus moves to the document (or the first `[autofocus]` element); back/forward restore the
  scroll position. `search.set()` keeps both.
- **Errors.** `notFound()` and unknown URLs render the nearest `_404` page of the SPA; other errors
  its `_error` page (`{ status, error }` props), with the layouts kept. A thrown `redirect()`
  navigates. Without such a page, a minimal built-in error page replaces the SPA.
- **`invalidate()`** from `lumen` re-runs the SPA's async components and resources (they keep
  their UI meanwhile) and resolves once they settled. `submit()` redirects navigate through the
  router, and a successful `submit()` invalidates (on MPA pages it does not: that would reload).
- **Stale modules.** A page module that fails to load (an old chunk after a deploy) loads the URL
  as a document instead.

## Example

```tsx check file=routes/music/_layout.tsx
// src/routes/music/_layout.tsx: an SPA under /music, with a persistent layout
import { href, type LayoutProps } from "lumen";
import { Link, navigating } from "lumen/router";

export const mode = "spa";

export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<"/music">) {
  return (
    <div class="app">
      <nav>
        <Link href={href("/music")}>Songs</Link>
        <Link href={href("/music/settings")} prefetch="viewport">
          Settings
        </Link>
      </nav>
      {navigating() && <progress />}
      <main>{props.children}</main>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/music/index.tsx
// src/routes/music/index.tsx: a filter kept in the query
import { search } from "lumen/router";

export default function Songs() {
  const query = () => search().get("q") ?? "";
  return (
    <input
      type="search"
      value={query()}
      onInput={(event) => search.set({ q: event.currentTarget.value || null }, { replace: true })}
    />
  );
}
```

```tsx check file=routes/music/settings.tsx
// src/routes/music/settings.tsx
import { href } from "lumen";
import { navigate } from "lumen/router";

export default function Settings() {
  return <button onClick={() => navigate(href("/music"), { replace: true })}>Done</button>;
}
```

See also: [Routing](../concepts/routing.md), [Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md),
[`lumen`: app layer](app.md).

<!-- source: reference/vite.md -->

# `lumen/vite`

> The Vite 8 plugin: compiles `.stsx` and `.tsx` with the Lumen compiler, picks the `lumen` entry per Vite environment, reports diagnostics in the overlay and reloads on edit.

## lumen()

```ts
import lumen from "lumen/vite";

function lumen(options?: LumenOptions): Plugin[];

interface LumenOptions {
  /** Modules compiled by Lumen. Default: .stsx and .tsx files. */
  include?: RegExp;
  /** Modules left to Vite. Default: anything in node_modules. */
  exclude?: RegExp;
  /** The project's default route mode; a layout's or route's `export const mode` overrides it. */
  mode?: "static" | "server" | "spa"; // default "static"
  /** Whether spa routes render their content on the server (false: the shell only). */
  ssr?: boolean; // default true
  /** Trailing slashes of page URLs: "always"/"never" redirect to the canonical form. */
  trailingSlash?: "ignore" | "always" | "never"; // default "ignore"
  /** The origin check of form posts (on by default); false turns it off. */
  csrf?: false | { allowedOrigins?: readonly string[] };
  /** `.svg` imports as inline components; false leaves them to Vite (URLs). */
  svg?: boolean | { optimize?: boolean | SvgoConfig; currentColor?: boolean }; // default true
  /** `.md` imports as components; the hook validates or transforms each file's frontmatter. */
  md?: boolean | { frontmatter?(data: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: { file: string }): unknown }; // default false
  /** `.html` imports as components. */
  html?: boolean; // default false
  /** Cross-document View Transitions between MPA pages (not under reduced motion). */
  viewTransitions?: boolean; // default false
  /** Speculation rules that prefetch the same-origin links of MPA pages. */
  prefetch?: "hover" | "viewport" | "none"; // default "hover"
  /** A strict Content Security Policy: nonces per response, hashes for prerendered pages. */
  csp?: "strict";
  /** Response headers: a record for every response, or rules by path (below base). */
  headers?: Record<string, string> | { path: string; headers: Record<string, string> }[];
}
```

The project options (`mode`, `ssr`, `trailingSlash`, `csrf`, `viewTransitions`, `prefetch`,
`headers`) are
read by `lumen dev`, `lumen build` and `lumen routes`/`check` from the plugin's `api.options`.
Invalid values and unknown option names throw when the config loads. `csp: "strict"` is
described in [Security](../concepts/security.md): nonces on every inline script and style Lumen
writes and on those written in JSX, static `style` strings as nonce'd rules, a `Content-Security-Policy` header for pages rendered per request, and a hash policy
`<meta>` in prerendered pages. `allowedOrigins` takes full
origins such as `"https://app.example.com"`, without a path or trailing slash.

**Response headers** (`headers`). Declare them once: a record applies to every response; rules
apply to the paths they match, below Vite's `base` (`*` matches one segment, `**` any number,
later rules win for the same header). `lumen dev`, `lumen preview` and `@lumen/adapter-node` send
them on every response, static files included, and `lumen build` writes them to
`dist/client/_headers`, the file Netlify and Cloudflare Pages read (`**` becomes `*`, a `*`
segment a `:name` placeholder). Headers that middleware, endpoints or `response().setHeader()` set
win.

```ts
lumen({
  headers: [
    { path: "/**", headers: { "cross-origin-opener-policy": "same-origin" } },
    { path: "/admin/**", headers: { "x-robots-tag": "noindex" } },
  ],
});
```

| Deployment                   | Where the headers come from                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumen dev`, `lumen preview` | `lumen({ headers })`                                                              |
| `@lumen/adapter-node`        | `lumen({ headers })`, from the build (`config.headers` of `dist/server/entry.js`) |
| Netlify, Cloudflare Pages    | `lumen({ headers })`, as `dist/client/_headers`                                   |
| Other static hosts and CDNs  | The host's own header configuration, copied from `lumen({ headers })`             |

Per-response headers that depend on the request belong in middleware or `response().setHeader()`.

MPA navigation ([Routing](../concepts/routing.md)): the page documents that `lumen dev` and
`lumen build` render get, in `<head>`:

- `viewTransitions: true`:
  `<style>@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){@view-transition{navigation:auto}}</style>`,
  on every page, `spa` pages included (their client navigations are not cross-document).
- `prefetch`: a `<script type="speculationrules">` on every page except `spa` pages, whose
  `<Link prefetch>` prefetches instead. It matches the links below Vite's `base` (`href_matches`),
  except the URLs of endpoints, with `moderate` eagerness for `"hover"` (the pointer rests on the
  link, or it is pressed) and `eager` for `"viewport"` (as soon as the browser sees fit: desktop
  Chromium on a brief hover, mobile Chromium as links enter the viewport); `"none"` emits nothing.
  On a page with `<Link prefetch>` links (marked `data-l-prefetch`), the rules give each level its
  own `selector_matches` rule, and the default's rule skips links marked otherwise; with `"none"`,
  only such pages get rules ([`lumen/router`](router.md#link)).

Both are inline elements: a Content-Security-Policy you set without `'unsafe-inline'` needs
`'inline-speculation-rules'` in `script-src` for the rules, and the hash of the `<style>` in
`style-src`.

What it does:

- Compiles Lumen modules before Vite's own transform, which is told to skip them. Server consumers
  (SSR) get `lumen/server` code; everything else gets `lumen/dom` code.
- Resolves `lumen` to its `browser` entry in client environments and its `node` entry in server
  environments, and keeps every `lumen` entry out of dependency pre-bundling, so compiled code and
  the runtime share one module instance. Under Vitest, tests in a DOM environment (`happy-dom`,
  `jsdom`) get the `browser` entry too (see [Testing](../concepts/testing.md)).
- Turns compiler diagnostics into Vite warnings and errors with code frames (the dev overlay).
- Loads project `.svg` files (`./icon.svg`, `./icon.svg?inline`) as inline components for the
  environment's target, optimised with SVGO (`optimize`: `true` for Lumen's defaults,
  `preset-default` plus `convertStyleToAttrs`; your SVGO config; or `false`). Scripts, event
  handlers and `javascript:` URLs are always removed and ids prefixed per file. `currentColor:
  true` replaces every colour with `currentColor` (SVGO's `convertColors`, before other
  plugins). `?url` and `?raw` stay Vite's, and `.svg` files in `exclude` (node_modules) keep
  Vite's URL import. See [SVG imports](../concepts/svg.md).
- With `md`/`html`, loads project `.md` and `.html` files as static components: their source
  becomes the Lumen module `<file>.md.stsx` (`.html.stsx`), compiled like any `.stsx` file, with
  `frontmatter` from `<file>.md?lumen-frontmatter`, `headings`, relative asset URLs as `?url`
  imports, and client scripts loaded by an island from `<file>.html?lumen-script`. HTML entries (`index.html`, HTML build inputs) and `public/` files
  stay Vite's. See [Markdown and HTML imports](../concepts/content.md).
- Hot updates: a client module that imports `mount` from `lumen/dom` (an app entry) accepts updates
  of every module it reaches and re-mounts the app into the same container. Component state resets;
  module-level signals of unchanged modules survive.
- Style blocks become `<file>?lumen&type=style&lang.css` modules handled by Vite's CSS pipeline.
  Modules that `$` references import constants from are tracked as dependencies of that CSS module.
  A style-only edit, or an edit to such a constants module, hot-updates the CSS without remounting.

> **Status:** compilation, environments, diagnostics, HMR, style-block CSS, `.svg`, `.md` and `.html` imports and the
> project options above are available. The designed options `adapter` and `css` are not.

## Example

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import lumen from "lumen/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [lumen({ mode: "server", exclude: /[\\/](node_modules|legacy)[\\/]/ })],
});
```

<!-- source: reference/jsx.md -->

# JSX types and tsconfig

> `lumen/jsx-runtime` types JSX for `jsxImportSource: "lumen"`; `lumen/env` declares the global `JSX` namespace, `import.meta.env` and `Locals`. This page lists the type rules and the tsconfig.

## tsconfig.json

A Lumen project's `tsconfig.json` extends the tsconfig that Lumen generates (decision-25). This is
what `create-lumen` writes, what `lumen agents init` writes when the file is missing, and what
`lumen check` prints when there is none:

```jsonc
{
  // Lumen's compiler options, shadow TSX and route types. lumen dev, build, check and typegen
  // write the generated file; add your own options below.
  "extends": "./.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json",
}
```

Add your own `compilerOptions` next to `extends`; they override the generated ones. `lumen check`,
`lumen typegen`, `lumen dev`/`build`, `lumen/vite` and the language server write
`.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json`, so it follows the installed Lumen version and the workspace
layout. `.lumen/` is not committed: in a fresh clone, run `lumen typegen` (or `lumen check`) before
a bare `tsc`.

The generated file, with paths relative to `.lumen/`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "lumen",
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "rootDirs": ["..", "./shadow"],
    "types": ["lumen/env"]
  },
  "include": ["../src", "./shadow", "./types"]
}
```

| Option                                        | Why                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `jsx: "preserve"`, `jsxImportSource: "lumen"` | The Lumen compiler transforms JSX; TypeScript only checks it against Lumen's types.       |
| `rootDirs` with `.lumen/shadow`               | `import "./X.stsx"` resolves to the shadow file `X.stsx.tsx`.                             |
| `include` `.lumen/shadow`, `.lumen/types`     | Shadow files and generated route types are part of the program.                           |
| `types: ["lumen/env"]`                        | The global `JSX` namespace, `import.meta.env`, `Locals` and `.svg`/`.md`/`.html` modules. |
| `allowImportingTsExtensions`                  | Imports name their extension: `./Card.stsx`, `./tokens.ts`.                               |
| `skipLibCheck`                                | `lumen/env` and `vite/client` can both be loaded: their `*.svg` declarations collide.     |

If you set `include` or `types` yourself, they replace the generated lists: keep `src`,
`.lumen/shadow` and `.lumen/types` in `include`, and `lumen/env` in `types`. An array `extends`
keeps a shared base: `["../../tsconfig.base.json", "./.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json"]` (later
entries win). `lumen check` reports missing options (`LUM6001`).

### Imports outside `src/` and `.stsx` from other packages

The generated `rootDirs` pair a _mirror base_ with `.lumen/shadow`. The mirror base is the nearest
directory that contains the project and the Lumen packages it uses. These are the linked
dependencies that list `lumen` as a dependency, plus the enclosing package of a project without its
own `package.json`. For a standalone project, it is the project root (`..` above).

Shadows mirror the paths below that base. For example, `apps/web/.lumen/shadow/apps/web/src/` holds
the app's own shadows and `apps/web/.lumen/shadow/packages/ui/src/` holds a package's. So a `.stsx`
import may leave `src/` (`../../lib/x.ts`), and a component that a workspace package re-exports
from its own `.stsx` files (`@acme/ui` → `./Button.stsx`) is type-checked with your project, with
errors pointing at its sources.

### Without `extends`

A tsconfig can also set the options itself:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "lumen",
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "rootDirs": ["src", ".lumen/shadow/src"],
    "types": ["lumen/env"]
  },
  "include": ["src", ".lumen/shadow", ".lumen/types"]
}
```

Its `rootDirs` pair only `src` with `.lumen/shadow/src`, so `.stsx` files must stay inside `src/`:
a `.stsx` import that leaves `src/` does not resolve (TS2307), and the `.stsx` modules of workspace
packages have no shadow. `lumen check` warns (`LUM6001`) when a used package has `.stsx` files that
the tsconfig's `rootDirs` leave out.

## The `JSX` namespace

| Type                                                        | Rule                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `JSX.Element`                                               | What JSX evaluates to: nodes, strings, numbers, booleans, `null`/`undefined`, arrays and functions of those.                                            |
| `JSX.ElementType`                                           | Intrinsic tags, and sync **or async** function components.                                                                                              |
| `JSX.IntrinsicElements`                                     | Every HTML (except `style`), SVG and MathML tag of lib.dom, plus custom elements (`my-widget`).                                                         |
| `JSX.IntrinsicAttributes`                                   | `key`, and on components `client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible` (`boolean \| string`), `client:media` (`string`), `client:only`.                |
| `JSX.ClassValue`                                            | `string \| false \| null \| undefined \| Record<string, boolean \| null \| undefined> \| ClassValue[]`.                                                 |
| `JSX.CSSProperties`                                         | Kebab-case CSS properties (`"font-weight"`, `"-webkit-line-clamp"`) and `--custom` properties; values `string \| number \| false \| null \| undefined`. |
| `JSX.EventHandler<E, T>`                                    | `(event: E & { currentTarget: T }) => void`.                                                                                                            |
| `JSX.Ref<T>`                                                | What `ref<T>()` returns: callable with the element, readable as `() => T \| undefined`.                                                                 |
| `JSX.HTMLProps<T>`, `JSX.SVGProps<T>`, `JSX.MathMLProps<T>` | Props of an element type, for wrappers.                                                                                                                 |

**Element props.** Every element accepts `children`, `class`, `style`, `ref`, `attach`, `innerHTML`,
`key`, its attributes, `onX` handlers and `on:x` listeners. `input` also accepts `bind:value`
(string or number signal) and `bind:checked` (boolean signal); `select` and `textarea` accept
`bind:value`.

**Rejected on purpose** (type errors with a hint): `className` (use `class`), `htmlFor` (use
`for`), camelCase `style` keys, exact-case or lowercase handlers (`onKeydown`, `onclick`), and
`<style>` in `.tsx` files.

**Event names.** `onX` handlers use React-style camelCase after `on` (`onClick`, `onKeyDown`,
`onDblClick`, `onPointerDown`, `onMouseEnter`); the DOM event is the suffix lowercased. Bubbling
events are delegated; non-bubbling ones (`focus`, `blur`, `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`,
`pointerenter`, `pointerleave`, `scroll`, `load`, `error`, media events) get a direct listener.
`on:name` adds a native listener with the exact name; any `on:${string}` is accepted for custom
events.

## Custom elements

Undeclared custom elements accept global attributes and any other attribute. Type one by
augmenting `IntrinsicElements`:

```tsx check
declare module "lumen/jsx-runtime" {
  namespace JSX {
    interface IntrinsicElements {
      "rating-stars": JSX.HTMLProps<HTMLElement> & { value: number; max?: number };
    }
  }
}

export function Review() {
  return (
    <rating-stars
      value={4}
      on:rating-change={(event: CustomEvent<number>) => console.log(event.detail)}
    />
  );
}
```

## `lumen/env`

```ts
interface ImportMetaEnv {
  readonly [publicVariable: `PUBLIC_${string}`]: string;
  BASE_URL: string;
  MODE: string;
  DEV: boolean;
  PROD: boolean;
  SSR: boolean;
}
declare module "lumen" {
  interface Locals {}
}
declare module "*.css" {} // import "./app.css": bundled into the page's CSS
declare module "*.css?url" {} // export default url: string
declare module "*.css?inline" {} // export default css: string
declare module "*.css?raw" {} // export default source: string
declare module "*.svg" {
  const Svg: (props: JSX.SVGProps<SVGSVGElement> & { title?: string }) => JSX.Element;
  export default Svg;
}
declare module "*.svg?inline" {} // the same component
declare module "*.svg?url" {} // export default url: string
declare module "*.svg?raw" {} // export default raw: string
declare module "*.md" {
  const Content: () => JSX.Element;
  export default Content;
  export interface Frontmatter extends Record<string, unknown> {} // merge your fields into it
  export const frontmatter: Frontmatter;
  export interface Heading {
    depth: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;
    text: string;
    id: string;
  } // read-only
  export const headings: ReadonlyArray<Heading>; // document order, ids of the rendered anchors
}
declare module "*.html" {
  const Content: () => JSX.Element;
  export default Content;
}
```

Declare known public variables by merging `interface ImportMetaEnv { readonly PUBLIC_API: string }`.
The built-in members match `vite/client`, so both can be loaded; list `lumen/env` first, because
`vite/client` types `*.svg` as a URL string and the first declaration wins. The two default exports
of `*.svg` are a duplicate in their `.d.ts` files, which `skipLibCheck` (generated) does not check (see
[SVG imports](../concepts/svg.md)). TypeScript 7 checks side-effect imports
(`noUncheckedSideEffectImports`), hence `*.css`. With `lumen/env` listed first it also matches
`*.module.css`, so a CSS module import has no class map type; scoped `<style>` blocks replace CSS
modules in Lumen components.

<!-- source: reference/cli.md -->

# CLI

> The `lumen` command: `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `check`, `typegen`, `routes`, `lint`, `fmt`, `docs`, `explain`, `agents init` and `mcp`, each with help, `--format json` and stable exit codes.

```sh
lumen <command> [options]
lumen <command> --help        # usage, options, exit codes and examples
lumen help --format json      # every command, for agents
```

## Output contract

- **Exit codes:** `0` success, `1` problems found (errors, unformatted files, nothing found, a
  failed build, a server that could not start), `2` the tool itself failed or was misused (unknown
  command or option, missing tsconfig or oxlint, a project root that does not exist). Each
  command's `--help` lists its exit codes.
- **`--format json`:** stdout carries one JSON document, `{ "command": "<name>", "ok": <bool>, ... }`.
  `ok` is `true` exactly when the exit code is `0`. When the command could not do its job and no
  diagnostics explain why, `failure: { message, help? }` says so. Fields are only ever added.
  Usage errors are reported the same way (`lumen chek --format json` prints `{ "command": "chek",
  "ok": false, "failure": {...}, "suggestions": ["check"] }`).
- **Logs** go to stderr with `--format json`, so stdout parses as JSON.
- **Typos** get suggestions: `lumen chek` prints `Did you mean "lumen check"?`.

| Option                   | Applies to   | Meaning                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--root <dir>`, `--cwd`  | all          | Project root (default: the current directory).                |
| `--format human \| json` | all          | Output format (default `human`).                              |
| `-h, --help`             | all          | Help for the command.                                         |
| `-v, --version`          |              | The version (`{ command: "version", ok, version }` in JSON).  |
| `-p, --project <file>`   | check        | tsconfig path relative to the root (default `tsconfig.json`). |
| `--check`                | fmt          | List unformatted files and exit 1 instead of writing.         |
| `--port <n>`             | dev, preview | Port; `0` picks a free one.                                   |
| `--host <addr>`          | dev, preview | Listen address (`0.0.0.0`: all addresses).                    |

## lumen dev

Starts the Vite dev server with SSR and HMR, until interrupted.

```sh
lumen dev --port 3000
lumen dev --format json   # one line once listening: { "command": "dev", "ok": true, "url": "http://localhost:5173/", "urls": { "local": [...], "network": [...] } }
```

Like Vite, the server stops when its stdin ends; start it with an open stdin when it runs in the
background.

## lumen build

Builds the client and server bundles into `dist/`, then prerenders the `static` routes. When every
route is prerendered (no `server` route, no server-rendered `spa` route, no form action), the build
removes `dist/server`: `dist/client` is the whole site, and `serverEntry` is `null`.
`lumen({ headers })` is written to `dist/client/_headers`.

```sh
lumen build --format json   # { outDir, clientDir, serverEntry, prerendered: [{ path, file, kind }] }
```

Route errors (`LUM5002`, `LUM5003`, `LUM5005`) and compile errors exit 1.

## lumen preview

Serves the build output until interrupted. With `dist/server`, it serves it with
`@lumen/adapter-node` (a dependency of the project), and the app runs with `NODE_ENV=production`
unless `NODE_ENV` is set. Without it (every route prerendered), it serves
`dist/client` as a static site, no adapter needed: page URLs map to `about/index.html` or
`about.html`, and unknown URLs get `404.html` with status 404, as static hosts do. Every response,
static files included, gets `lumen({ headers })` and Vite's `preview.headers`, which default to
`server.headers` (as with `vite preview`)
([adapter `headers`](./adapter-node.md#createhandler)).
`--format json` prints one line once listening: `{ "command": "preview", "ok": true, "url" }`.

## lumen check

Type-checks the project: runs typegen (`.lumen/types/routes.d.ts`), writes shadow TSX files for
every `.stsx` (`.lumen/shadow/`; also those of used Lumen packages when the tsconfig extends
`.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json`, as the template does, see
[tsconfig](./jsx.md#imports-outside-src-and-stsx-from-other-packages)), writes the generated
tsconfig, runs `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, maps shadow positions back
to the `.stsx` sources (same line and UTF-16 column), and merges scanner, route, tsconfig and
compiler diagnostics for `.stsx` and `.tsx` files (such as `LUM1006` for a `<style>` block in a
`.tsx` file). For style diagnostics, the modules that `$` constants are imported from are resolved
like TypeScript resolves them (relative paths, tsconfig `paths`, package `exports`). Route
diagnostics use the project's default mode from `lumen({ mode })`.

```sh
lumen check
lumen check --format json   # { command, ok, diagnostics: [...], summary: { errors, warnings, hints, files } }
```

Each JSON diagnostic has `source` (`ts`, `lumen`, `oxlint`, `stylelint`), `code`, `severity`,
`file`, `line`, `column`, `endLine`, `endColumn`, `message`, and optional `help`, `docs` and
`fix`. A `fix` is `{ message, edits: [{ line, column, endLine, endColumn, text }] }`, with the same
positions as diagnostics; apply all its edits together.

TypeScript errors inside a raw-CSS `<style>` block of a `.tsx` file are dropped: `LUM1006` reports
the block, and renaming the file to `.stsx` removes them. TypeScript errors on an island call site
for a prop that cannot be serialized are reported as `LUM4002` on the prop (see
[LUM4002](../errors/LUM4002.md)). While the project has syntax errors, TypeScript reports no type
errors yet: the report then ends with a note (JSON: `notes: [...]`), and another run after the
fixes shows them.

## lumen typegen

Writes the route types (`.lumen/types/routes.d.ts`), the generated tsconfig
(`.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json`) and syncs the shadow TSX files (`.lumen/shadow/`), without
type-checking: what a bare `tsc` or an editor needs.

```sh
lumen typegen --format json   # { routeTypes: { file, changed }, routes, shadows: { dir, files, written, deleted }, diagnostics, summary }
```

## lumen routes

Lists the routes in match order, with their kind, mode (from the route, its layouts or the project
default `lumen({ mode })`) and layouts. `spa (shell)` marks a `spa` page with `ssr = false`.

```sh
$ lumen routes
Routes in src/routes (default mode: static): 2 pages, 1 endpoint

PATTERN        KIND      MODE    FILE                LAYOUTS
/              page      static  index.stsx          _layout.stsx
/api/search    endpoint  server  api/search.ts
/blog/[slug]   page      server  blog/[slug].stsx    _layout.stsx, blog/_layout.stsx

$ lumen routes --format json   # { routesDir, defaultMode, routes: [{ pattern, file, kind, mode, ssr?, layouts, params }], diagnostics, summary }
```

Paths in JSON are project-relative. Exits 1 when the routes have errors.

## lumen lint

Runs oxlint on the project, including `.stsx` files (through their shadow TSX, with diagnostics
inside style blocks dropped), and, when the project installs and configures stylelint, on each
block's CSS with `$` references replaced by same-length identifiers. The JSON report has the shape
of `lumen check`'s.

## lumen fmt

```sh
lumen fmt [paths...]        # default path: src
lumen fmt --check
lumen fmt --check --format json   # { check, files: [{ file, status, warnings, error? }], summary: { files, formatted, errors } }
```

Formats `.stsx` files: the TSX with oxfmt (each block replaced by a placeholder), then each block's
CSS separately with its `$` references protected, then re-indents and stitches the file together.
With `--check`, a `formatted` file is one that is not formatted yet.

## lumen docs

```sh
lumen docs                  # the docs index
lumen docs signals          # a topic by name...
lumen docs concepts/signals # ...or by path
lumen docs LUM2001          # a diagnostic page (also errors/LUM2001, diagnostics/LUM2001)
lumen docs fetchJSON        # an exported name: its section of the API reference
lumen docs bind:value       # no topic matches: search, best matches first
lumen docs --format json    # { topics: [{ topic, title, summary }] }
lumen docs signals --format json   # { topic, title, summary, related, content }
lumen docs Link --format json      # { topic, heading, content }
lumen docs "await island" --format json   # { query, results: [{ topic, title, score, snippet }] }
```

Prints the version-matched docs from `node_modules/lumen/docs`. A bare name prefers concepts over
reference pages and lists the other matches. An exported name (case-sensitive, such as `signal`,
`Link` or `fail`) prints the section of the reference page that documents it. A search requires
every term to occur in a page.
Exits 1 when nothing matches.

## lumen explain

```sh
lumen explain LUM3010
lumen explain lum3010 --format json   # { code, title, severity, category, topic, content }
```

Prints the long-form explanation of a diagnostic code: what it means, an example, and how to fix
it. Exits 1 for an unknown code and 2 for text that is not a code.

## lumen agents init

```sh
lumen agents init
lumen agents init --mcp           # also .mcp.json (Claude Code) and .codex/config.toml (Codex)
lumen agents init --format json   # { files: [{ file, action: "created" | "updated" | "unchanged" }] }
```

Makes an existing project agent-ready, as `create-lumen` does for new ones: a Lumen section in
`AGENTS.md` (between `<!-- lumen:start … -->` and `<!-- lumen:end -->`, pointing at
`node_modules/lumen/docs`, the `.stsx` format, the key rules and `lumen check`), a `CLAUDE.md`
that references `@AGENTS.md`, the `lumen` skill (`.claude/skills/lumen/SKILL.md`) and the
`*.stsx linguist-language=TSX` line in `.gitattributes`, and a `tsconfig.json` that extends
`.lumen/tsconfig.generated.json` when the project has none (an existing one is left alone).
Re-running it updates only those parts. `--mcp` also registers `lumen mcp` for Claude Code and
Codex, run with the package manager of the lockfile (see [MCP](mcp.md#register-it)); the JSON
report then has `mcp: { command, args, note }`.

## lumen mcp

```sh
lumen mcp
claude mcp add lumen -- npx lumen mcp   # register it with Claude Code
```

Starts the MCP server on stdio for coding agents: the tools `docs_search`, `docs_get`, `check`,
`routes`, `components`, `compile`, `render` and `dev_logs`, and the docs and the route manifest as
resources. It runs until the client disconnects. See [MCP server](mcp.md).

## Planned commands

`lumen upgrade` is designed (spec §3) but not available yet.

<!-- source: reference/mcp.md -->

# MCP server

> `lumen mcp` serves the project to coding agents over the Model Context Protocol: version-matched docs, `lumen check` diagnostics with fixes, routes, component metadata, compiler output, server-rendered HTML and dev server logs.

`lumen mcp` starts a stdio MCP server for the project in the current directory (or `--root`). It
gives an agent the same answers as the CLI, as structured tool results, without parsing terminal
output. Related: [CLI](cli.md), [Compiler and diagnostics](../concepts/compiler.md).

## Register it

The agent starts the server itself. `create-lumen --mcp` (new projects) and
`lumen agents init --mcp` (existing ones) register it for both Claude Code and Codex, run with the
project's package manager (`npx lumen mcp`, `pnpm exec lumen mcp`, `yarn lumen mcp` or
`bunx lumen mcp`, from the lockfile):

- `.mcp.json`: the `lumen` entry of `mcpServers` (Claude Code's project servers; it asks once
  before starting them). Other servers in the file are kept.
- `.codex/config.toml`: an `[mcp_servers.lumen]` table. Codex reads project config only in
  trusted projects; otherwise register it with `codex mcp add` as below. The rest of the file is
  kept.

Or by hand, once in the project directory:

```sh
# Claude Code (add --scope project to write .mcp.json and share it with the team)
claude mcp add lumen -- npx lumen mcp

# Codex
codex mcp add lumen -- npx lumen mcp
```

Agents configured with a JSON file (Claude Code's `.mcp.json`, Cursor's `.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lumen": { "command": "npx", "args": ["lumen", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "lumen": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["lumen", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

The server runs until the agent disconnects. It exits with `2` when the project root does not
exist. stdout carries the protocol; console output of app code goes to stderr and to `dev_logs`.

## Tools

| Tool          | Input                                                 | Returns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docs_search` | `query`, `limit?` (10)                                | `{ query, results: [{ topic, title, summary, score, snippet }] }`, best first; every term must occur in a page.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `docs_get`    | `topic`                                               | The page as Markdown. A topic is a path (`concepts/signals`), a bare name (`signals`), a code (`LUM2001`) or `""` for the index. An exported name (`fetchJSON`) returns its reference section.                                                                               |
| `check`       | `files?`, `project?`                                  | `lumen check` as `{ ok, summary, diagnostics, notes? }`. With `files`, only their diagnostics, and `projectSummary` for the whole project.                                                                                                                                   |
| `routes`      | none                                                  | `lumen routes --format json`: `{ routesDir, defaultMode, routes: [{ pattern, file, kind, mode, ssr?, layouts, params }], diagnostics, summary }`.                                                                                                                            |
| `components`  | `file?`                                               | `{ files: [{ file, components, islands, fileScope, hasStyles, errors }] }` for one file, or for every `.stsx`/`.tsx` file under `src/`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `compile`     | `file?` or `source`, `target?` (`both`)               | `{ file, client: { code, css, cssDeps }, server: { code }, diagnostics }`: what the Vite plugin compiles, without source maps.                                                                                                                                               |
| `render`      | `path`, `method?`, `headers?`, `maxLength?`, `strip?` | `{ url, status, headers, body, truncated }` from an in-process dev server. Redirects are returned, not followed. `strip: true` returns only the visible markup of an HTML page (no scripts, styles, link/meta tags, templates, hydration comments or `data-l-*` attributes). |
| `dev_logs`    | `since?`, `level?`, `limit?` (100)                    | `{ available, entries: [{ id, time, level, source, message }] }`: the logs of the dev server that `render` started.                                                                                                                                                          |

- **Diagnostics** (`check`, `compile`, `components`) have the shape of `lumen check --format json`:
  `source`, `code`, `severity`, `file`, 1-based `line`/`column`/`endLine`/`endColumn`, `message`,
  and optional `help`, `docs` (a topic for `docs_get`) and `fix`. A `fix` is
  `{ message, edits: [{ line, column, endLine, endColumn, text }] }`; apply all its edits together.
- **Components** list each component's `name`, `exported`, `async`, `location`, `props` and
  `styleScopes`. `props` is the first parameter as written (`{ parameter: "props: CardProps" }`),
  plus the `type` declaration when the props type is an interface or type alias of the same file;
  it is `null` for a component without props. `styleScopes` are the `data-l-*` attributes of the
  elements that hold `<style>` blocks. `islands` are the file's `client:*` call sites with their
  `ref`, `module`, `export` and `strategy`.
- **`compile`** takes the file's text from `source` when given (the file need not exist), and
  folds `$` constants imported from other modules like the build does.
- **`render`** starts the dev server on first use, on a free port of `127.0.0.1`, and keeps it
  running: later calls see file changes like `lumen dev` does. Pages return their HTML; endpoints
  their response body. Render errors return the dev error page, and their details are in
  `dev_logs`.
- **`dev_logs`** returns `available: false` with an explanation until `render` started the dev
  server: the logs of a `lumen dev` started in a terminal are not visible to the MCP server. Pass
  the last `id` you saw as `since` to read only newer entries; `level` is the minimum (`info`,
  `warn`, `error`); `source` is `vite` (the dev server and Lumen's plugins) or `console` (app
  code).

## Resources

| URI                    | Content                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lumen://docs/<topic>` | Each docs page as Markdown, e.g. `lumen://docs/concepts/signals`. |
| `lumen://routes`       | The route manifest, as the `routes` tool returns it (JSON).       |

## Workflow for agents

1. Look the feature up: `docs_search`, then `docs_get` (the docs match the installed version).
2. Make the change.
3. `check` and fix every error; `docs_get` with a diagnostic's `docs` topic explains it.
4. `render` the affected routes to see the HTML; `dev_logs` with `level: "warn"` shows problems.

<!-- source: reference/adapter-node.md -->

# `@lumen/adapter-node`

> Serves a `lumen build` output with Node: the static files of `dist/client` first, then the app's request handler from `dist/server/entry.js`, with streamed responses.

`lumen preview` uses it, so a project that previews or deploys on Node depends on it. Concepts:
[Rendering modes](../concepts/rendering-modes.md) (build output), [Server](../concepts/server.md).

## createServer

```ts
function createServer(options?: ServerOptions): Promise<LumenServer>;

interface ServerOptions extends HandlerOptions {
  /** Default: the `PORT` env variable, else 3000. `0` picks a free port. */
  port?: number;
  /** Default: the `HOST` env variable, else every address. */
  host?: string;
}

interface LumenServer {
  readonly server: import("node:http").Server;
  /** The URL it listens on, e.g. `http://localhost:3000/` (with the app's `base`). */
  readonly url: string;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

Loads the build and starts an HTTP server; resolves once it listens. A missing build fails with
"No build in dist … Run `lumen build` first."

**`NODE_ENV`.** A build runs in production: `createServer` and `createHandler` set
`process.env.NODE_ENV` to `"production"` when it is unset, before they load the build, so the
app and every library it imports (many branch on `NODE_ENV`) see it from their first line. An
explicit value is kept (`NODE_ENV=staging node server.ts`). `dist/server/entry.js` does the same
when another server imports it directly.

## createHandler

```ts
function createHandler(options?: HandlerOptions): Promise<NodeHandler>;

interface HandlerOptions {
  /** The build output directory, holding `client/` and `server/entry.js`. Default: `dist`. */
  dir?: string | URL;
  /** The public origin (`https://example.com`) behind a proxy. Default: `ORIGIN`, else the request's. */
  origin?: string;
  /** `ctx.env` and `env()` of requests. Default: `process.env`. */
  env?: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
  /** Headers for every response; a response's own header of the same name wins. */
  headers?: import("node:http").OutgoingHttpHeaders;
  /** Compress responses for clients that accept brotli or gzip. Default: true. */
  compress?: boolean;
}

type NodeHandler = (
  req: IncomingMessage,
  res: ServerResponse,
  next?: (error?: unknown) => void,
) => void;
```

The same request handling as a Node request listener, for your own `http.createServer` or as
connect/Express middleware (errors go to `next`). Set `origin` (or `ORIGIN`) when a proxy terminates
TLS or rewrites the host: request URLs, and the cross-site check of form posts, use it.

`headers` go on every response, the static files (prerendered pages included) and the app's
alike: the place for headers that middleware cannot add to static files, such as
`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy` for a cross-origin isolated page.
They are set first, so a response's own header of the same name wins: a static file's
`cache-control`, a page's `response().setHeader()`, a middleware's response. `lumen preview` passes
Vite's `preview.headers`, which default to `server.headers`. The build's `lumen({ headers })`
([lumen/vite](./vite.md#lumen)) apply too, by path, after these: prefer them, so dev, preview,
this adapter and static hosts send the same headers.
